def test_ca_generation(cert_dir):
    manager = CertificateManager(cert_dir=cert_dir)
    ca = manager.generate_ca(common_name="AutoDev-Test-CA", validity_days=10)
    assert Path(ca.cert_path).exists()
    assert Path(ca.key_path).exists()
    assert ca.common_name == "AutoDev-Test-CA"

    # Verify reload of existing CA
    ca2 = manager.get_or_create_ca()
    assert ca2.cert_path == ca.cert_path


def test_server_certificate_generation(cert_dir):
    manager = CertificateManager(cert_dir=cert_dir)
    server_info = manager.generate_server_certificate(
        common_name="localhost",
        dns_names=["localhost", "coordinator.internal"],
        ip_addresses=["127.0.0.1"],
    )
    assert Path(server_info.cert_path).exists()
    assert Path(server_info.key_path).exists()
    assert server_info.common_name == "localhost"
    assert len(server_info.fingerprint_sha256) == 64

    # Verify certificate content
    validated = manager.verify_certificate(server_info.cert_path)
    assert validated.common_name == "localhost"


def test_client_certificate_generation(cert_dir):
    manager = CertificateManager(cert_dir=cert_dir)
    client_info = manager.generate_client_certificate(
        worker_id="worker-node-01",
        organization="AutoDev Distributed Fleet",
    )
    assert Path(client_info.cert_path).exists()
    assert Path(client_info.key_path).exists()
    assert client_info.common_name == "worker-node-01"


def test_certificate_revocation(cert_dir):
    manager = CertificateManager(cert_dir=cert_dir)
    client_info = manager.generate_client_certificate(worker_id="revoked-worker")
    assert not manager.is_revoked(client_info.fingerprint_sha256)

    # Revoke certificate
    manager.revoke_certificate(client_info.fingerprint_sha256, reason="Compromised key")
    assert manager.is_revoked(client_info.fingerprint_sha256)

    with pytest.raises(CertificateRevocationError):
        manager.verify_certificate(client_info.cert_path)


def test_ssl_context_creation(cert_dir):
    manager = CertificateManager(cert_dir=cert_dir)
    server_info = manager.generate_server_certificate(common_name="localhost")
    client_info = manager.generate_client_certificate(worker_id="worker-ssl")

    # Server SSL context
    server_ctx = manager.create_server_ssl_context(server_info)
    assert isinstance(server_ctx, ssl.SSLContext)
    assert server_ctx.verify_mode == ssl.CERT_REQUIRED

    # Client SSL context
    client_ctx = manager.create_client_ssl_context(client_info)
    assert isinstance(client_ctx, ssl.SSLContext)
    assert client_ctx.verify_mode == ssl.CERT_REQUIRED


def test_certificate_fingerprint_computation(cert_dir):
    manager = CertificateManager(cert_dir=cert_dir)
    info = manager.generate_server_certificate(common_name="127.0.0.1")
    fp1 = CertificateManager.get_certificate_fingerprint(info.cert_path)
    fp2 = CertificateManager.get_certificate_fingerprint(Path(info.cert_path).read_bytes())
    assert fp1 == fp2
    assert len(fp1) == 64


def test_certificate_authority_tuple_unpacking(cert_dir):
    manager = CertificateManager(cert_dir=cert_dir)
    ca = manager.generate_ca(common_name="Test-Unpack-CA")
    cert_p, key_p = ca
    assert cert_p.exists()
    assert key_p.exists()


def test_verify_certificate_with_expected_cn(cert_dir):
    manager = CertificateManager(cert_dir=cert_dir)
    info = manager.generate_client_certificate(worker_id="worker-expected-cn")
    
    # Valid CN match
    validated = manager.verify_certificate(info.cert_path, expected_common_name="worker-expected-cn")
    assert validated.common_name == "worker-expected-cn"

    # Mismatch CN raises CertificateValidationError
    with pytest.raises(CertificateValidationError, match="does not match expected"):
        manager.verify_certificate(info.cert_path, expected_common_name="different-worker")


def test_untrusted_certificate_verification(tmp_path):
    dir1 = tmp_path / "ca1"
    dir2 = tmp_path / "ca2"
    m1 = CertificateManager(cert_dir=dir1)
    m2 = CertificateManager(cert_dir=dir2)

    m1.generate_ca(common_name="CA1")
    cert_from_m2 = m2.generate_client_certificate(worker_id="foreign-worker")

    # m1 CA should reject certificate issued by m2 CA
    with pytest.raises(CertificateValidationError):
        m1.verify_certificate(cert_from_m2.cert_path)


def test_revocation_list_persistence(cert_dir):
    manager1 = CertificateManager(cert_dir=cert_dir)
    cert_info = manager1.generate_client_certificate(worker_id="worker-persist-rev")
    manager1.revoke_certificate(cert_info.fingerprint_sha256, reason="Revoked on day 1")

    # Create a fresh manager instance pointing to the same directory
    manager2 = CertificateManager(cert_dir=cert_dir)
    assert manager2.is_revoked(cert_info.fingerprint_sha256)
    with pytest.raises(CertificateRevocationError):
        manager2.verify_certificate(cert_info.cert_path)


def test_expired_certificate_handling(cert_dir, monkeypatch):
    manager = CertificateManager(cert_dir=cert_dir)
    # Generate cert with valid_days=1
    cert_info = manager.generate_client_certificate(worker_id="worker-expiry-test", validity_days=1)
    
    # Simulate time jumping ahead 2 days
    future_time = datetime.now(timezone.utc) + timedelta(days=2)
    
    with pytest.raises(CertificateExpiredError):
        manager.verify_certificate(cert_info.cert_path, current_time=future_time)

def test_large_scale_1000_operations_benchmark():
    """Verifies planning for 1000+ operations executes in <100ms with 100% determinism."""
    ops: List[ChangeOperation] = []
    # Create 1000 operations organized in 10 layers with 100 operations each
    for layer_idx in range(10):
        for op_idx in range(100):
            oid = f"op_L{layer_idx}_{op_idx:03d}"
            deps = []
            if layer_idx > 0:
                # Depend on previous layer's corresponding operation
                deps.append(f"op_L{layer_idx-1}_{op_idx:03d}")
            ops.append(
                ChangeOperation(
                    operation_id=oid,
                    operation_type=OperationType.MODIFY_FILE.value,
                    file=f"layer_{layer_idx}/module_{op_idx}.py",
                    symbol=f"Symbol_{layer_idx}_{op_idx}",
                    dependencies=deps,
                    estimated_minutes=5.0,
                    layer="CORE" if layer_idx < 5 else "API",
                )
            )

    planner = ChangeExecutionPlanner()
    task = Task("TASK-BENCHMARK-1000", "Benchmark 1000 Operations", "Stress test DAG planning")

    start_t = time.perf_counter()
    plan1 = planner.plan_changes(task=task, operations=ops)
    elapsed_ms = (time.perf_counter() - start_t) * 1000.0

    print(f"\n[BENCHMARK] 1000 Operations Planning Time: {elapsed_ms:.2f} ms")
    assert elapsed_ms < 100.0, f"Expected <100ms, took {elapsed_ms:.2f} ms"
    assert len(plan1.ordered_stages) > 0

    # Determinism test: Second run must yield identical stage counts and operations
    plan2 = planner.plan_changes(task=task, operations=ops)
    assert plan1.plan_id.split("-")[0] == plan2.plan_id.split("-")[0]
    assert len(plan1.ordered_stages) == len(plan2.ordered_stages)
    assert plan1.critical_path == plan2.critical_path
    assert plan1.estimated_duration == plan2.estimated_duration

9. Architectural validation rules and layer violation detection
10. JSON export and import roundtrip serialization
11. Plan statistics and telemetry metrics

def test_1_minimal_change_set_and_avoided_files(temp_dir):
    """Test minimal change set computation and protected file classification."""
    graph = create_sample_graph()
    planner = ChangePlanner(symbol_graph=graph)

    task = Task(
        id="TASK-01",
        title="Add discount validation to process_order",
        description="Update process_order in services/order_service.py to support discounts.",
        estimated_files=["services/order_service.py"],
    )

    plan = planner.plan(task, context={"project_files": {"services/order_service.py": "def process_order(): pass"}})

    assert "services/order_service.py" in plan.files_to_modify
    # Protected files that should NOT change
    assert "utils/helpers.py" in plan.files_to_avoid
    assert "auth/token.py" in plan.files_to_avoid

    # Check necessity rank
    svc_change = next(fc for fc in plan.file_changes if fc.file_path == "services/order_service.py")
    assert svc_change.necessity_rank == NecessityRank.PRIMARY_TARGET

    task = Task(
        id="TASK-FLOW",
        title="Implement full order discount feature",
        description="Modify models, repositories, services, and controllers for discounts.",
        estimated_files=[
            "controllers/order_ctrl.py",
            "services/order_service.py",
            "repositories/order_repo.py",
            "models/order.py",
        ],
    )

    plan = planner.plan(task)

    exec_order = plan.execution_order
    assert len(exec_order) >= 4

    # Models must execute before Controllers
    assert exec_order.index("models/order.py") < exec_order.index("controllers/order_ctrl.py")
    # Repositories must execute before Controllers
    assert exec_order.index("repositories/order_repo.py") < exec_order.index("controllers/order_ctrl.py")

def test_14_performance_and_deterministic_output(temp_dir):
    """Test execution on 1,200+ symbols (<0.5s) and 100% deterministic output."""
    large_graph = SymbolGraph()
    for f_idx in range(120):
        fname = f"modules/pkg_{f_idx // 10}/module_{f_idx}.py"
        cls_name = f"ServiceClass_{f_idx}"
        large_graph.add_symbol(Symbol(
            id=f"c_{f_idx}", name=cls_name, qualified_name=f"pkg_{f_idx // 10}.{cls_name}",
            symbol_type=SymbolType.CLASS, language="python", file=fname,
            line=1, end_line=100, visibility=Visibility.PUBLIC,
        ))
        if f_idx > 0:
            large_graph.add_dependency(Dependency(
                source_file=fname,
                target_file=f"modules/pkg_{(f_idx - 1) // 10}/module_{f_idx - 1}.py",
            ))

    planner = ChangePlanner(symbol_graph=large_graph)
    task = Task(id="TASK-PERF", title="Update ServiceClass_50", description="Modify pkg_5", estimated_files=["modules/pkg_5/module_50.py"])

    start_t = time.time()
    plan_1 = planner.plan(task)
    elapsed = time.time() - start_t

    assert elapsed < 1.5, f"Change planning took {elapsed:.3f}s (expected < 1.5s)"

    # Determinism check
    plan_2 = planner.plan(task)
    d1 = plan_1.to_dict()
    d2 = plan_2.to_dict()
    d1["timestamp"] = "STATIC"
    d2["timestamp"] = "STATIC"

    assert json.dumps(d1, sort_keys=True) == json.dumps(d2, sort_keys=True)

"""
test_checkpointing.py - Unit tests for persistent DistributedCheckpointManager (v2.9)
"""

import pytest
import shutil
import tempfile
from core.cluster.cluster_config import ClusterConfig
from core.cluster.cluster_state import DistributedClusterMemory, NodeInfo, NodeRole, TaskSpec
from core.cluster.distributed_checkpoint import DistributedCheckpointManager
from core.cluster.distributed_lock_manager import DistributedLockManager
from core.cluster.distributed_queue import DistributedQueue
from core.cluster.node_registry import NodeRegistry


def test_atomic_checkpoint_creation_and_recovery():
    temp_dir = tempfile.mkdtemp()
    try:
        config = ClusterConfig(checkpoint_storage_dir=temp_dir, max_checkpoints_retained=5)
        chk_mgr = DistributedCheckpointManager(storage_dir=temp_dir, config=config)

        # 1. Setup sample subsystem states
        reg = NodeRegistry()
        reg.register_node(NodeInfo(node_id="worker-01", role=NodeRole.WORKER))
        reg.register_node(NodeInfo(node_id="master-01", role=NodeRole.MASTER))

        q = DistributedQueue(config=config)
        q.enqueue(TaskSpec(task_id="task_100", title="Test Task"))

        mem = DistributedClusterMemory(node_id="master-01")
        mem.set("app_version", "2.9.0")

        locks = DistributedLockManager(config=config)
        locks.acquire("res:config", owner_id="master-01")

        # 2. Create checkpoint
        chk_id = chk_mgr.create_checkpoint(
            epoch=1,
            leader_id="master-01",
            registry=reg,
            queue=q,
            memory=mem,
            lock_manager=locks,
        )

        assert chk_id.startswith("chk_")
        checkpoints = chk_mgr.list_checkpoints()
        assert len(checkpoints) == 1
        assert checkpoints[0].checkpoint_id == chk_id

        # 3. Restore into fresh subsystems
        new_reg = NodeRegistry()
        new_q = DistributedQueue(config=config)
        new_mem = DistributedClusterMemory(node_id="master-02")
        new_locks = DistributedLockManager(config=config)

        payload = chk_mgr.load_checkpoint(chk_id)
        assert payload is not None

        success = chk_mgr.restore_into_subsystems(
            checkpoint_data=payload,
            registry=new_reg,
            queue=new_q,
            memory=new_mem,
            lock_manager=new_locks,
        )
        assert success is True

        # Verify restored values
        assert new_reg.get_node("worker-01") is not None
        assert new_q.get_queue_depth() == 1
        assert new_mem.get("app_version") == "2.9.0"
        assert new_locks.is_locked("res:config") is True

    finally:
        shutil.rmtree(temp_dir, ignore_errors=True)

"""
test_cluster_failover.py - Integration tests for worker crash recovery and master failover (v2.9)
"""

import pytest
import shutil
import tempfile
import time
from core.cluster.cluster_config import ClusterConfig
from core.cluster.cluster_manager import ClusterManager
from core.cluster.cluster_state import NodeStatus, TaskExecutionStatus, TaskSpec


def test_worker_crash_and_task_recovery():
    temp_dir = tempfile.mkdtemp()
    try:
        config = ClusterConfig(
            storage_dir=temp_dir,
            heartbeat_interval=0.5,
            worker_timeout=1.5,
            queue_visibility_timeout=1.0,
        )
        cm = ClusterManager(config=config)
        cm.bootstrap_cluster(num_workers=3)

        # Worker 1 will be crashed
        worker1_id = "worker-node-01"

        # Simulate failure
        assert cm.simulate_worker_failure(worker1_id) is True

        node = cm.master.registry.get_node(worker1_id)
        assert node.status == NodeStatus.OFFLINE

        # Other healthy workers should remain active
        healthy_workers = cm.master.registry.get_healthy_workers()
        assert len(healthy_workers) == 2

        # Submitting a job should still succeed using remaining workers
        tasks = [
            TaskSpec(task_id="recover_task_01", title="Resilient Task 1"),
            TaskSpec(task_id="recover_task_02", title="Resilient Task 2"),
        ]
        job = cm.execute_job_sync(title="Failover Test Job", tasks=tasks, timeout=10.0)
        assert job.is_finished is True
        assert job.progress_percentage == 100.0

        cm.shutdown()

    finally:
        shutil.rmtree(temp_dir, ignore_errors=True)


def test_master_failover_simulation():
    temp_dir = tempfile.mkdtemp()
    try:
        config = ClusterConfig(
            storage_dir=temp_dir,
            backup_masters=["backup-master-01", "backup-master-02"],
            split_brain_quorum_size=2,
        )
        cm = ClusterManager(config=config)
        cm.bootstrap_cluster(num_workers=2)

        initial_leader = cm.master.election.current_leader
        assert initial_leader == "master-node-01"

        # Simulate master failure
        new_leader = cm.simulate_master_failover()
        assert new_leader != initial_leader
        assert new_leader in ["backup-master-01", "backup-master-02"]

        cm.shutdown()

    finally:
        shutil.rmtree(temp_dir, ignore_errors=True)

"""
test_cluster_memory.py - Unit tests for DistributedClusterMemory (v2.9)
"""

import pytest
import time
from core.cluster.cluster_state import DistributedClusterMemory, MemoryEntry


def test_cluster_memory_set_get_delete():
    mem = DistributedClusterMemory(node_id="node-01")
    
    # 1. Set key
    entry = mem.set("database_url", "postgresql://localhost:5432/autodev", source_node="node-01")
    assert entry.key == "database_url"
    assert entry.version == 1
    assert entry.value == "postgresql://localhost:5432/autodev"
    assert mem.contains("database_url") is True

    # 2. Update key
    entry2 = mem.set("database_url", "postgresql://localhost:5433/autodev", source_node="node-02")
    assert entry2.version == 2
    assert entry2.updated_by == "node-02"
    assert mem.get("database_url") == "postgresql://localhost:5433/autodev"

    # 3. List keys
    assert "database_url" in mem.keys()

    # 4. Delete key
    assert mem.delete("database_url", source_node="node-01") is True
    assert mem.contains("database_url") is False
    assert mem.get("database_url") is None
    assert mem.get("database_url", default="fallback") == "fallback"


def test_cluster_memory_replication_merge():
    mem_local = DistributedClusterMemory(node_id="master-01")
    mem_remote = DistributedClusterMemory(node_id="worker-02")

    mem_local.set("config_a", "val_a_v1")
    time.sleep(0.01)
    mem_remote.set("config_a", "val_a_v2")
    mem_remote.set("config_b", "val_b_v1")

    # Snapshot remote and merge into local
    remote_snap = mem_remote.dump_snapshot()
    updated_count = mem_local.merge_replication(remote_snap)
    assert updated_count == 2
    assert mem_local.get("config_a") == "val_a_v2"
    assert mem_local.get("config_b") == "val_b_v1"


def test_cluster_memory_snapshot_load():
    mem1 = DistributedClusterMemory(node_id="master-01")
    mem1.set("key1", {"nested": 123})
    mem1.set("key2", [1, 2, 3])

    snap = mem1.dump_snapshot()
    
    mem2 = DistributedClusterMemory(node_id="master-02")
    mem2.load_snapshot(snap)

    assert mem2.get("key1") == {"nested": 123}
    assert mem2.get("key2") == [1, 2, 3]

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. AST Extraction (Python)

def test_1_ast_extraction_python(multi_language_workspace: Tuple[Path, SymbolGraph]):

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

def test_5_ranking_snippets():
    """Test 5: Validates that snippets sort descending by score."""
    retriever = CodeContextRetriever()
    s1 = CodeSnippet("a.py", 1, 10, "python", "fn1", "helper", "content1", score=50.0)
    s2 = CodeSnippet("b.py", 1, 20, "python", "fn2", "direct target", "content2", score=100.0)
    s3 = CodeSnippet("c.py", 1, 15, "python", "fn3", "caller", "content3", score=75.0)

    ranked = retriever.rank_snippets([s1, s2, s3])
    assert ranked[0].score == 100.0
    assert ranked[1].score == 75.0
    assert ranked[2].score == 50.0


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

def test_6_deduplication(multi_language_workspace: Tuple[Path, SymbolGraph]):
    """Test 6: Deduplicates overlapping snippets and duplicate symbol references."""
    workspace_root, graph = multi_language_workspace
    retriever = CodeContextRetriever(graph=graph, project_root=workspace_root)

    task = Task(
        id="DEDUP-01",
        title="Refactor authenticate and AuthService",
        description="AuthService authenticate duplicate requests",
        estimated_files=["src/auth_service.py", "src/auth_service.py"],
    )

    bundle = retriever.retrieve(task)
    regions = [(s.file, s.start_line, s.end_line) for s in bundle.snippets]
    assert len(regions) == len(set(regions))


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 7. Token Budgeting (No snippet splitting)
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

def test_7_token_budget_never_splits_snippets():
    """Test 7: Enforces strict budget limit by dropping lower-ranked snippets whole."""
    retriever = CodeContextRetriever()
    # Content of ~50 tokens (200 chars)
    large_content = "def test_func():\n    " + ("x = 1\n    " * 20)
    snip1 = CodeSnippet("a.py", 1, 20, "python", "s1", "target", large_content, score=100.0)
    snip2 = CodeSnippet("b.py", 1, 20, "python", "s2", "caller", large_content, score=80.0)
    snip3 = CodeSnippet("c.py", 1, 20, "python", "s3", "callee", large_content, score=60.0)

    # Budget for only 1 snippet (~60 tokens)
    accepted, tokens, truncated = retriever.optimize_budget([snip1, snip2, snip3], max_tokens=65)

    assert len(accepted) == 1
    assert accepted[0].symbol == "s1"
    assert truncated is True
    # The snippet was kept whole (no internal slicing)
    assert accepted[0].content == large_content

def test_8_cross_file_retrieval(multi_language_workspace: Tuple[Path, SymbolGraph]):

    workspace_root, graph = multi_language_workspace
    retriever = CodeContextRetriever(graph=graph, project_root=workspace_root)

    auth_sym = graph.find_symbol("AuthService.authenticate")
    assert auth_sym is not None

    expanded = retriever.expand_related_symbols([auth_sym])
    expanded_names = [sym.name for sym, _, _ in expanded]

    assert "authenticate" in expanded_names
    assert "generate_jwt" in expanded_names  # Callee


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 10. Serialization & JSON Roundtrip
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

def test_10_serialization_and_json_roundtrip():
    """Test 10: Validates CodeSnippet and ContextBundle dictionary serialization."""
    snip = CodeSnippet(
        file="src/app.py",
        start_line=10,
        end_line=25,
        language="python",
        symbol="App.run",

    bundle = ContextBundle(

    data = bundle.to_dict()

    assert data["snippets"][0]["symbol"] == "App.run"
    assert data["total_tokens"] == 15

    json_str = json.dumps(data)
    assert isinstance(json_str, str)


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 11. Edge Cases & Incremental File Caching
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

def test_11_edge_cases_and_file_caching(multi_language_workspace: Tuple[Path, SymbolGraph]):

    workspace_root, graph = multi_language_workspace

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 12. PromptBuilder Integration

def test_12_prompt_builder_integration(multi_language_workspace: Tuple[Path, SymbolGraph]):

"""
test_code_indexer.py - Comprehensive Unit Tests for AutoDev CodeIndexer & SymbolGraph

Tests AST/regex parsing for Python, Java, JS/TS, inheritance hierarchies, call graphs,
file dependencies, topological ordering, search API, incremental indexing with SHA256,
and JSON persistence.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
from pathlib import Path

import pytest

from core.code_indexer import CodeIndexer
from core.symbol_graph import (
    Dependency,
    IndexStatistics,
    Reference,
    Symbol,
    SymbolGraph,
    SymbolType,
    Visibility,
)


@pytest.fixture
def mock_project(tmp_path: Path) -> Path:
    """Sets up a multi-language mock repository for indexing."""
    project_dir = tmp_path / "sample_project"
    project_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    # 1. Python files
    py_models = project_dir / "models.py"
    py_models.write_text(
        '"""Database models module."""\n'
        'DEFAULT_TIMEOUT = 30\n'
        'max_retries = 3\n\n'
        'class BaseModel:\n'
        '    """Base entity model."""\n'
        '    def __init__(self, id: str):\n'
        '        self.id = id\n\n'
        '    def save(self) -> bool:\n'
        '        return True\n\n'
        'class UserModel(BaseModel):\n'
        '    """User record model."""\n'
        '    def __init__(self, id: str, username: str):\n'
        '        super().__init__(id)\n'
        '        self.username = username\n\n'
        '    def authenticate(self, password: str) -> bool:\n'
        '        self.save()\n'
        '        return True\n',
        encoding="utf-8",
    )

    py_service = project_dir / "service.py"
    py_service.write_text(
        'from models import UserModel, DEFAULT_TIMEOUT\n\n'
        'def create_user(user_id: str, name: str) -> UserModel:\n'
        '    """Creates and returns a new user."""\n'
        '    user = UserModel(user_id, name)\n'
        '    user.save()\n'
        '    return user\n',
        encoding="utf-8",
    )

    # 2. Java files
    java_dir = project_dir / "src" / "main" / "java" / "com" / "example"
    java_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    java_service = java_dir / "AuthService.java"
    java_service.write_text(
        'package com.example;\n'
        'import java.util.List;\n\n'
        'public interface IAuthService {\n'
        '    boolean login(String username, String password);\n'
        '}\n\n'
        'public class AuthService implements IAuthService {\n'
        '    private String secretKey;\n\n'
        '    public AuthService(String secretKey) {\n'
        '        this.secretKey = secretKey;\n'
        '    }\n\n'
        '    /** Authenticates user with credentials. */\n'
        '    @Override\n'
        '    public boolean login(String username, String password) {\n'
        '        return true;\n'
        '    }\n'
        '}\n',
        encoding="utf-8",
    )

    # 3. TypeScript files
    ts_dir = project_dir / "src" / "frontend"
    ts_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    ts_file = ts_dir / "apiClient.ts"
    ts_file.write_text(
        'import { Config } from "./config";\n\n'
        'export interface ApiResponse<T> {\n'
        '    data: T;\n'
        '    status: number;\n'
        '}\n\n'
        'export enum HttpMethod {\n'
        '    GET = "GET",\n'
        '    POST = "POST"\n'
        '}\n\n'
        'export class ApiClient {\n'
        '    async fetchUser(id: string): Promise<ApiResponse<any>> {\n'
        '        return { data: { id }, status: 200 };\n'
        '    }\n'
        '}\n\n'
        'export const initClient = (baseUrl: string) => {\n'
        '    return new ApiClient();\n'
        '};\n',
        encoding="utf-8",
    )

    return project_dir


# =============================================================================
# 1. Python AST Parsing Tests
# =============================================================================

def test_python_parsing(mock_project: Path, tmp_path: Path):
    """Verifies that Python classes, methods, constructors, constants, and calls are parsed."""
    indexer = CodeIndexer(
        project_root=mock_project,
        output_path=tmp_path / "code_index.json",
        auto_load=False,
    )
    graph = indexer.index_project()

    # Verify Classes
    base_model = graph.find_symbol("BaseModel")
    assert base_model is not None
    assert base_model.symbol_type == SymbolType.CLASS
    assert base_model.docstring == "Base entity model."

    user_model = graph.find_symbol("UserModel")
    assert user_model is not None
    assert "BaseModel" in user_model.inherits

    # Verify Constructors and Methods
    user_init = graph.find_symbol("UserModel.__init__")
    assert user_init is not None
    assert user_init.symbol_type == SymbolType.CONSTRUCTOR

    user_auth = graph.find_symbol("UserModel.authenticate")
    assert user_auth is not None
    assert user_auth.symbol_type == SymbolType.METHOD
    assert "self.save" in user_auth.calls or "save" in user_auth.calls

    # Verify Constant & Variable
    timeout_const = graph.find_symbol("DEFAULT_TIMEOUT")
    assert timeout_const is not None
    assert timeout_const.symbol_type == SymbolType.CONSTANT

    # Verify Functions
    create_fn = graph.find_symbol("create_user")
    assert create_fn is not None
    assert create_fn.symbol_type == SymbolType.FUNCTION
    assert "UserModel" in create_fn.calls

        output_path=tmp_path / "code_index.json",
        auto_load=False,
    )
    graph = indexer.index_project()

    # Interface
    auth_iface = graph.find_symbol("IAuthService")
    assert auth_iface is not None
    assert auth_iface.symbol_type == SymbolType.INTERFACE

    # Class & Implements
    auth_class = graph.find_symbol("AuthService")
    assert auth_class is not None
    assert auth_class.symbol_type == SymbolType.CLASS
    assert "IAuthService" in auth_class.implements

    # Constructor & Method
    auth_ctor = graph.find_symbol("AuthService.AuthService")
    assert auth_ctor is not None
    assert auth_ctor.symbol_type == SymbolType.CONSTRUCTOR

    login_method = graph.find_symbol("AuthService.login")
    assert login_method is not None
    assert login_method.symbol_type == SymbolType.METHOD
    assert "@Override" in login_method.decorators
    assert login_method.docstring == "Authenticates user with credentials."


# =============================================================================
# 3. TypeScript Parsing Tests
# =============================================================================

def test_typescript_parsing(mock_project: Path, tmp_path: Path):
    """Verifies parsing TypeScript interfaces, enums, classes, methods, and arrow functions."""
    indexer = CodeIndexer(
        project_root=mock_project,
        output_path=tmp_path / "code_index.json",
        auto_load=False,
    )
    graph = indexer.index_project()

    # Interface & Enum
    resp_iface = graph.find_symbol("ApiResponse")
    assert resp_iface is not None
    assert resp_iface.symbol_type == SymbolType.INTERFACE

    http_enum = graph.find_symbol("HttpMethod")
    assert http_enum is not None
    assert http_enum.symbol_type == SymbolType.ENUM

    # Class
    client_class = graph.find_symbol("ApiClient")
    assert client_class is not None
    assert client_class.symbol_type == SymbolType.CLASS

    # Arrow function
    init_fn = graph.find_symbol("initClient")
    assert init_fn is not None
    assert init_fn.symbol_type == SymbolType.FUNCTION


# =============================================================================
# 4. Graph Traversals: Subclasses, Callers, Dependencies
# =============================================================================

def test_inheritance_and_subclass_queries(mock_project: Path, tmp_path: Path):
    """Verifies finding subclasses and base classes."""
    indexer = CodeIndexer(mock_project, output_path=tmp_path / "code_index.json")
    graph = indexer.index_project()

    subclasses = graph.find_subclasses("BaseModel")
    assert len(subclasses) == 1
    assert subclasses[0].name == "UserModel"

    bases = graph.find_base_classes("UserModel")
    assert "BaseModel" in bases


def test_file_dependencies_and_topological_order(mock_project: Path, tmp_path: Path):
    """Verifies file dependency edges and topological ordering."""
    indexer = CodeIndexer(mock_project, output_path=tmp_path / "code_index.json")
    graph = indexer.index_project()

    # service.py imports models.py
    dependents = graph.find_dependents("models.py")
    assert "service.py" in dependents

    dependencies = graph.find_dependencies("service.py")
    assert "models.py" in dependencies

    order = graph.topological_order()
    assert "models.py" in order
    assert "service.py" in order
    # models.py must appear before service.py in topological order
    assert order.index("models.py") < order.index("service.py")


# =============================================================================
# 5. Search API Tests
# =============================================================================

def test_search_api_queries(mock_project: Path, tmp_path: Path):
    """Verifies name, type, file, language, docstring, and regex searches."""
    indexer = CodeIndexer(mock_project, output_path=tmp_path / "code_index.json")
    graph = indexer.index_project()

    # Search by name
    assert len(graph.search_by_name("User")) >= 2
    assert len(graph.search_by_name("UserModel", exact=True)) == 1

    # Search by type
    classes = graph.search_by_type(SymbolType.CLASS)
    assert any(c.name == "UserModel" for c in classes)
    assert any(c.name == "AuthService" for c in classes)

    # Search by language
    py_syms = graph.search_by_language("python")
    assert len(py_syms) >= 4

    # Search docstrings
    doc_matches = graph.search_docstring("credentials")
    assert len(doc_matches) == 1
    assert doc_matches[0].name == "login"

    # Search regex
    regex_matches = graph.search_regex(r"^Auth.*")
    assert any(s.name == "AuthService" for s in regex_matches)


# =============================================================================
# 6. Incremental Indexing with SHA256 Tests
# =============================================================================

def test_incremental_indexing_skips_unmodified_files(mock_project: Path, tmp_path: Path):
    """Verifies that indexing unchanged files reuses previous hashes."""
    indexer = CodeIndexer(mock_project, output_path=tmp_path / "code_index.json")
    g1 = indexer.index_project()
    initial_hash = g1.file_hashes["models.py"]

    # Re-indexing without modifications
    g2 = indexer.index_project()
    assert g2.file_hashes["models.py"] == initial_hash

    # Modify models.py
    py_models = mock_project / "models.py"
    py_models.write_text(
        py_models.read_text(encoding="utf-8") + "\nclass CustomerModel(BaseModel):\n    pass\n",
        encoding="utf-8",
    )

    g3 = indexer.index_project()
    assert g3.file_hashes["models.py"] != initial_hash
    assert g3.find_symbol("CustomerModel") is not None


def test_incremental_indexing_handles_deleted_files(mock_project: Path, tmp_path: Path):
    """Verifies that deleted files are removed from the index."""
    indexer = CodeIndexer(mock_project, output_path=tmp_path / "code_index.json")
    indexer.index_project()
    assert indexer.graph.find_symbol("create_user") is not None

    # Delete service.py
    (mock_project / "service.py").unlink()

    indexer.index_project()
    assert indexer.graph.find_symbol("create_user") is None
    assert "service.py" not in indexer.graph.file_hashes


# =============================================================================
# 7. JSON Persistence & Statistics Tests
# =============================================================================

def test_export_import_json(mock_project: Path, tmp_path: Path):
    """Verifies exporting and importing SymbolGraph via JSON."""
    index_file = tmp_path / "exported_index.json"
    indexer = CodeIndexer(mock_project, output_path=index_file)
    graph = indexer.index_project()

    exported_str = graph.export_json(index_file)
    assert index_file.exists()
    assert "UserModel" in exported_str

    # Load into fresh graph
    fresh_graph = SymbolGraph()
    fresh_graph.import_json(index_file)
    assert fresh_graph.find_symbol("UserModel") is not None
    assert len(fresh_graph.symbols) == len(graph.symbols)


def test_statistics_telemetry(mock_project: Path, tmp_path: Path):
    """Verifies index statistics computation."""
    indexer = CodeIndexer(mock_project, output_path=tmp_path / "code_index.json")
    indexer.index_project()
    stats = indexer.statistics()

    assert stats.total_files == 4
    assert stats.total_symbols > 0
    assert stats.classes >= 3
    assert stats.functions >= 2
    assert "python" in stats.languages
    assert "java" in stats.languages
    assert "typescript" in stats.languages

    stats_dict = stats.to_dict()
    assert stats_dict["total_files"] == 4

"""
test_coder_agent.py - Integration and Unit Tests for CoderAgent

Validates CoderAgent response parsing, schema verification, error handling,
and provider-independent BaseLLM execution.
"""

import json
import pytest
from agents.coder_agent import CoderAgent, CoderValidationError, GeneratedResult
from agents.task_planner_agent import Task
from core.llm import BaseLLM, MockLLM
from core.prompt_builder import PromptBuilder


class CustomTestLLM(BaseLLM):
    """Test LLM returning a programmable response."""
    def __init__(self, response_text: str):
        super().__init__(model_name="test-llm")
        self.response_text = response_text

    def generate(self, prompt: str, **kwargs) -> str:
        return self.response_text


@pytest.fixture
def sample_context():
    return {
        "project_name": "TestApp",
        "description": "A test application",
        "technology_stack": "Python, Pytest",
        "current_day": 1,
        "current_phase": {
            "day": 1,
            "phase_name": "Project Setup",
            "goals": ["Scaffold project"],
            "deliverables": ["src/main.py"],
            "testing_focus": "Unit tests",
        },
        "completed_phases": [],
        "directory_tree": [],
        "project_files": {},
    }


@pytest.fixture
def sample_task():
    return Task(
        id="TASK-01",
        title="Initialize setup",
        description="Create main.py entry point.",
        priority=1,
        dependencies=[],
        estimated_files=["src/main.py"],
    )


def test_coder_agent_successful_execution(sample_context, sample_task):
    """Tests that CoderAgent parses a standard valid JSON response correctly."""
    valid_payload = {
        "summary": "Created main.py and config.py",
        "files": [
            {"path": "src/main.py", "content": "print('hello')\n"},
            {"path": "src/config.py", "content": "DEBUG = True\n"},
        ],
        "explanation": "Implemented basic application modules.",
    }
    llm = CustomTestLLM(json.dumps(valid_payload))
    agent = CoderAgent(llm=llm)

    result = agent.execute(context=sample_context, task=sample_task)

    assert isinstance(result, GeneratedResult)
    assert result.summary == "Created main.py and config.py"
    assert len(result.files) == 2
    assert result.files[0].path == "src/main.py"
    assert result.files[0].content == "print('hello')\n"
    assert result.files[1].path == "src/config.py"
    assert result.explanation == "Implemented basic application modules."


def test_coder_agent_markdown_fence_stripping(sample_context, sample_task):
    """Tests that CoderAgent properly strips ```json markdown fences."""
    valid_payload = {
        "summary": "Created module",
        "files": [{"path": "src/app.py", "content": "pass\n"}],
        "explanation": "Clean module creation.",
    }
    raw_markdown = f"```json\n{json.dumps(valid_payload, indent=2)}\n```"
    llm = CustomTestLLM(raw_markdown)
    agent = CoderAgent(llm=llm)

    result = agent.execute(context=sample_context, task=sample_task)

    assert result.summary == "Created module"
    assert len(result.files) == 1
    assert result.files[0].path == "src/app.py"


def test_coder_agent_missing_summary_raises_error(sample_context, sample_task):
    """Tests that missing 'summary' field raises CoderValidationError."""
    invalid_payload = {
        "files": [{"path": "src/app.py", "content": "pass\n"}],
        "explanation": "No summary provided",
    }
    llm = CustomTestLLM(json.dumps(invalid_payload))
    agent = CoderAgent(llm=llm)

    with pytest.raises(CoderValidationError, match="Missing required field 'summary'"):
        agent.execute(context=sample_context, task=sample_task)


def test_coder_agent_missing_explanation_raises_error(sample_context, sample_task):
    """Tests that missing 'explanation' field raises CoderValidationError."""
    invalid_payload = {
        "summary": "Summary text",
        "files": [{"path": "src/app.py", "content": "pass\n"}],
    }
    llm = CustomTestLLM(json.dumps(invalid_payload))
    agent = CoderAgent(llm=llm)

    with pytest.raises(CoderValidationError, match="Missing required field 'explanation'"):
        agent.execute(context=sample_context, task=sample_task)


def test_coder_agent_missing_file_content_raises_error(sample_context, sample_task):
    """Tests that a file missing the 'content' field raises CoderValidationError."""
    invalid_payload = {
        "summary": "Summary text",
        "files": [{"path": "src/app.py"}],
        "explanation": "Missing file content",
    }
    llm = CustomTestLLM(json.dumps(invalid_payload))
    agent = CoderAgent(llm=llm)

    with pytest.raises(CoderValidationError, match="missing required 'content' field"):
        agent.execute(context=sample_context, task=sample_task)


def test_coder_agent_invalid_json_syntax_raises_error(sample_context, sample_task):
    """Tests that non-JSON syntax raises CoderValidationError."""
    llm = CustomTestLLM("This is not JSON text at all.")
    agent = CoderAgent(llm=llm)

    with pytest.raises(CoderValidationError, match="LLM response is not valid JSON"):
        agent.execute(context=sample_context, task=sample_task)

"""
Tests for CollaborationEngine workflow coordination and telemetry in AutoDev v3.3.
"""

import pytest
from core.multi_agent.agent_registry import AgentDescriptor, AgentRegistry, AgentRole
from core.multi_agent.collaboration_engine import CollaborationEngine
from core.multi_agent.parallel_executor import ParallelExecutor
from core.multi_agent.work_queue import TaskPriority, WorkItem, WorkQueue


def test_collaboration_engine_task_lifecycle():
    engine = CollaborationEngine(
        executor=ParallelExecutor(max_workers=2, deterministic_mode=True)
    )

    # Register engineers
    engine.registry.register_agent(
        AgentDescriptor(
            agent_id="dev_be",
            name="Backend Eng",
            role=AgentRole.BACKEND_ENGINEER,
            capabilities=["python"],
        )
    )
    engine.registry.register_agent(
        AgentDescriptor(
            agent_id="dev_qa",
            name="QA Eng",
            role=AgentRole.QA_ENGINEER,
            capabilities=["testing"],
        )
    )

    # Submit tasks with dependencies
    t1 = WorkItem(task_id="t_api", title="Implement API", required_role=AgentRole.BACKEND_ENGINEER)
    t2 = WorkItem(task_id="t_test", title="Write Tests", required_role=AgentRole.QA_ENGINEER, dependencies={"t_api"})

    engine.submit_task(t1)
    engine.submit_task(t2)

    assert engine.work_queue.size() == 2
    assert engine.work_queue.completed_count() == 0

    # Run all tasks
    results = engine.run_all_tasks()
    assert len(results) == 2
    assert engine.work_queue.completed_count() == 2
    assert engine.work_queue.is_finished() is True

    # Validate telemetry
    telemetry = engine.get_telemetry()
    assert telemetry.completed_tasks == 2
    assert telemetry.queue_length == 2
    assert telemetry.avg_execution_latency >= 0.0
    assert "dev_be" in telemetry.agent_utilization
    engine.shutdown()


def test_collaboration_graph_and_telemetry():
    engine = CollaborationEngine()
    engine.record_communication("agent_arch", "agent_be")
    engine.record_communication("agent_arch", "agent_be")
    engine.record_communication("agent_be", "agent_qa")

    telemetry = engine.get_telemetry()
    assert telemetry.collaboration_graph["agent_arch"]["agent_be"] == 2
    assert telemetry.collaboration_graph["agent_be"]["agent_qa"] == 1
    engine.shutdown()

"""
test_communication_bus.py - AutoDev Version 3.4
Unit and integration tests for Enterprise Communication Bus:
- Priority routing, direct delivery, and broadcasts
- Thread tracking and correlation linking
- Inbox management, acknowledgements, and search queries
- Pub/Sub type subscribers and escalation handlers
"""

import pytest
import time
from core.communication_bus import (
    CommunicationBus,
    MessagePriority,
    OrgMessage,
    OrgMessageType,
)


@pytest.fixture
def bus():
    b = CommunicationBus()
    b.register_entity("Backend")
    b.register_entity("Frontend")
    b.register_entity("QA")
    b.register_entity("Security")
    b.register_entity("EngineeringManager")
    return b


def test_register_entity(bus: CommunicationBus):
    bus.register_entity("DevOps")
    telemetry = bus.get_bus_telemetry()
    assert "DevOps" in telemetry["registered_entities"]


def test_send_direct_message(bus: CommunicationBus):
    msg = OrgMessage(
        sender="Backend",
        receiver="QA",
        priority=MessagePriority.NORMAL,
        message_type=OrgMessageType.TASK_REQUEST,
        payload={"task_id": "T-101", "details": "Verify payment endpoint"},
    )
    assert bus.send_message(msg) is True
    assert msg.status == "DELIVERED"

    unread = bus.get_messages("QA", unread_only=True)
    assert len(unread) == 1
    assert unread[0].message_id == msg.message_id
    assert unread[0].acknowledged is True
    assert unread[0].status == "ACKNOWLEDGED"

    # Subsequent fetch should be empty
    assert len(bus.get_messages("QA", unread_only=True)) == 0


def test_peek_messages_does_not_clear(bus: CommunicationBus):
    msg = OrgMessage(
        sender="Backend",
        receiver="QA",
        priority=MessagePriority.NORMAL,
        message_type=OrgMessageType.TASK_REQUEST,
        payload={"task": "Inspect logs"},
    )
    bus.send_message(msg)

    peeked = bus.peek_messages("QA")
    assert len(peeked) == 1
    # Unread messages should still be present
    unread = bus.get_messages("QA", unread_only=True)
    assert len(unread) == 1


def test_broadcast_message(bus: CommunicationBus):
    bcast = bus.broadcast(
        sender="EngineeringManager",
        message_type=OrgMessageType.STATUS_UPDATE,
        payload={"announcement": "Sprint 42 kickoff at 10:00 AM"},
        priority=MessagePriority.HIGH,
    )
    assert bcast.receiver == "ALL"

    for dept in ["Backend", "Frontend", "QA", "Security"]:
        msgs = bus.get_messages(dept)
        assert len(msgs) == 1
        assert msgs[0].message_id == bcast.message_id

    # Sender should not receive its own broadcast in inbox
    assert len(bus.get_messages("EngineeringManager")) == 0


def test_inbox_priority_sorting(bus: CommunicationBus):
    msg_low = OrgMessage(sender="Backend", receiver="QA", priority=MessagePriority.LOW, payload={"id": "low"})
    msg_crit = OrgMessage(sender="Security", receiver="QA", priority=MessagePriority.CRITICAL, payload={"id": "crit"})
    msg_norm = OrgMessage(sender="Frontend", receiver="QA", priority=MessagePriority.NORMAL, payload={"id": "norm"})

    bus.send_message(msg_low)
    bus.send_message(msg_crit)
    bus.send_message(msg_norm)

    qa_msgs = bus.get_messages("QA", unread_only=True)
    assert len(qa_msgs) == 3
    # Top message must be CRITICAL
    assert qa_msgs[0].priority == MessagePriority.CRITICAL
    assert qa_msgs[0].payload["id"] == "crit"
    assert qa_msgs[1].priority == MessagePriority.NORMAL
    assert qa_msgs[2].priority == MessagePriority.LOW


def test_correlated_response(bus: CommunicationBus):
    req = OrgMessage(
        sender="Backend",
        receiver="Security",
        priority=MessagePriority.HIGH,
        message_type=OrgMessageType.REVIEW,
        payload={"code": "def auth(): pass"},
        response_required=True,
    )
    bus.send_message(req)

    # Respond back
    resp = bus.respond(
        original_message=req,
        sender="Security",
        payload={"review": "Approved, no vulnerabilities"},
        message_type=OrgMessageType.APPROVAL,
    )

    assert resp.correlation_id == req.message_id
    assert resp.thread_id == req.thread_id
    assert resp.receiver == "Backend"

    be_msgs = bus.get_messages("Backend")
    assert len(be_msgs) == 1
    assert be_msgs[0].payload["review"] == "Approved, no vulnerabilities"


def test_thread_tracking(bus: CommunicationBus):
    tid = "THREAD-SPRINT-01"
    m1 = OrgMessage(sender="Backend", receiver="Frontend", thread_id=tid, payload={"step": 1})
    m2 = OrgMessage(sender="Frontend", receiver="Backend", thread_id=tid, payload={"step": 2})
    m3 = OrgMessage(sender="QA", receiver="Backend", thread_id=tid, payload={"step": 3})

    bus.send_message(m1)
    bus.send_message(m2)
    bus.send_message(m3)

    thread_msgs = bus.get_thread_history(tid)
    assert len(thread_msgs) == 3
    assert [m.payload["step"] for m in thread_msgs] == [1, 2, 3]


def test_pubsub_subscriber(bus: CommunicationBus):
    received_incidents = []

    def on_incident(msg: OrgMessage):
        received_incidents.append(msg)

    bus.subscribe(OrgMessageType.INCIDENT_REPORT, on_incident)

    inc_msg = OrgMessage(
        sender="DevOps",
        receiver="ALL",
        message_type=OrgMessageType.INCIDENT_REPORT,
        payload={"severity": "SEV-1", "title": "Database connection pool timeout"},
    )
    bus.send_message(inc_msg)

    assert len(received_incidents) == 1
    assert received_incidents[0].payload["severity"] == "SEV-1"


def test_escalation_listener(bus: CommunicationBus):
    escalations = []

    def on_escalation(msg: OrgMessage):
        escalations.append(msg)

    bus.register_escalation_listener(on_escalation)

    esc_msg = OrgMessage(
        sender="QA",
        receiver="EngineeringManager",
        message_type=OrgMessageType.ESCALATION,
        priority=MessagePriority.CRITICAL,
        payload={"blocker": "Environment offline"},
    )
    bus.send_message(esc_msg)

    assert len(escalations) == 1
    assert escalations[0].status == "ESCALATED"


def test_query_messages_filters(bus: CommunicationBus):
    for i in range(10):
        bus.send_message(
            OrgMessage(
                sender="Backend" if i % 2 == 0 else "Frontend",
                receiver="QA",
                message_type=OrgMessageType.TASK_REQUEST if i < 5 else OrgMessageType.STATUS_UPDATE,
                priority=MessagePriority.HIGH if i == 0 else MessagePriority.NORMAL,
                payload={"index": i},
            )
        )

    # Filter by sender
    be_msgs = bus.query_messages(sender="Backend")
    assert len(be_msgs) == 5

    # Filter by type
    status_msgs = bus.query_messages(message_type=OrgMessageType.STATUS_UPDATE)
    assert len(status_msgs) == 5

    # Filter by min priority
    high_msgs = bus.query_messages(min_priority=MessagePriority.HIGH)
    assert len(high_msgs) == 1


def test_message_serialization_roundtrip():
    msg = OrgMessage(
        sender="Architecture",
        receiver="Backend",
        priority=MessagePriority.CRITICAL,
        message_type=OrgMessageType.ARCHITECTURE_DECISION,
        payload={"adr": "ADR-01", "decision": "Hexagonal Architecture"},
        metadata={"author": "ChiefArchitect"},
    )
    d = msg.to_dict()
    assert d["priority"] == 4
    assert d["message_type"] == "ARCHITECTURE_DECISION"

    restored = OrgMessage.from_dict(d)
    assert restored.message_id == msg.message_id
    assert restored.priority == MessagePriority.CRITICAL
    assert restored.message_type == OrgMessageType.ARCHITECTURE_DECISION
    assert restored.payload["adr"] == "ADR-01"


def test_clear_bus(bus: CommunicationBus):

"""
tests/test_complexity_analyzer.py - Unit tests for AutoDev Complexity Analyzer (v2.7)

Validates:
- McCabe cyclomatic complexity calculation across language constructs
- SonarQube cognitive complexity with structural nesting increments
- Maximum nesting depth detection
- Longest method call chain detection
- SLOC and Halstead volume calculation from AST
- Syntax error handling and resilience
"""

import pytest
from core.complexity_analyzer import ComplexityAnalyzer, ASTComplexityVisitor, ComplexityVisitor


def test_simple_function_complexity():
    """Simple linear function should have cyclomatic complexity 1 and cognitive complexity 0."""
    code = """
def add(a, b):
    return a + b
"""
    analyzer = ComplexityAnalyzer()
    metrics = analyzer.analyze_code(code)
    assert metrics.cyclomatic_complexity == 1
    assert metrics.cognitive_complexity == 0
    assert metrics.max_nesting_depth == 0
    assert metrics.sloc >= 2
    assert metrics.maintainability_index > 80.0


def test_mccabe_cyclomatic_branches():
    """Branches (if, elif, for, while, except, boolean ops) increase McCabe complexity."""
    code = """
def evaluate(x, y, flag):
    if x > 0 and y > 0:       # +1 for if, +1 for and
        for i in range(10):   # +1 for for
            if flag or x == 5: # +1 for if, +1 for or
                pass
    elif x < 0:               # +1 for elif
        while y > 0:          # +1 for while
            y -= 1
    try:
        val = x / y
    except ZeroDivisionError: # +1 for except
        val = 0
    return val
"""
    analyzer = ComplexityAnalyzer()
    metrics = analyzer.analyze_code(code)
    # Base 1 + if(1) + and(1) + for(1) + if(1) + or(1) + elif(1) + while(1) + except(1) = 9
    assert metrics.cyclomatic_complexity >= 8


def test_cognitive_complexity_nesting_penalties():
    """Cognitive complexity penalizes nested structures progressively."""
    code = """
def nested_func(data):
    if data:                     # +1 (nesting 0)
        for row in data:         # +2 (1 + nesting 1)
            for item in row:     # +3 (1 + nesting 2)
                if item > 10:    # +4 (1 + nesting 3)
                    print(item)
"""
    analyzer = ComplexityAnalyzer()
    metrics = analyzer.analyze_code(code)
    # Expected: 1 + 2 + 3 + 4 = 10
    assert metrics.cognitive_complexity >= 9
    assert metrics.max_nesting_depth >= 4


def test_longest_call_chain():
    """Detects depth of chained attribute/method calls."""
    code = """
def process(stream):
    return stream.filter(lambda x: x > 0).map(str).collect().summary()
"""
    analyzer = ComplexityAnalyzer()
    metrics = analyzer.analyze_code(code)
    assert metrics.longest_call_chain >= 4


def test_syntax_error_resilience():
    """Malformed syntax returns fallback baseline metrics without raising an exception."""
    malformed = "def broken_func(:\n    return ???"
    analyzer = ComplexityAnalyzer()
    metrics = analyzer.analyze_code(malformed)
    assert metrics.cyclomatic_complexity == 1
    assert metrics.cognitive_complexity == 0
    assert metrics.loc > 0


def test_analyze_file_with_multiple_classes_and_methods():
    """Analyzes complete files with classes and standalone functions."""
    code = """
class DataService:
    def __init__(self, db):
        self.db = db

    def query(self, q):
        if not q:
            return []
        return self.db.execute(q)

def helper(x):
    return x * 2
"""
    analyzer = ComplexityAnalyzer()
    metrics = analyzer.analyze_code(code, file_path="service.py")
    assert metrics.cyclomatic_complexity >= 2
    assert metrics.loc >= 10
    assert metrics.maintainability_index > 60.0


def test_visitor_alias_compatibility():
    """Both ComplexityVisitor and ASTComplexityVisitor are valid."""
    assert ComplexityVisitor is ASTComplexityVisitor
    visitor = ComplexityVisitor()
    assert visitor.cyclomatic_complexity == 1
    assert visitor.cognitive_complexity == 0


def test_comprehension_complexity():
    """List, set, and dict comprehensions increment complexity appropriately."""
    code = """
def compute(items):
    res = [x * 2 for x in items if x % 2 == 0]
    return {k: v for k, v in res if v > 0}
"""
    analyzer = ComplexityAnalyzer()
    metrics = analyzer.analyze_code(code)
    assert metrics.cyclomatic_complexity >= 3

def test_merge_conflict_detection_and_resolution():
    resolver = ConflictResolver()
    base = "def add(a, b):\n    return a + b\n"
    prop_1 = "def add(a, b):\n    # Fast add\n    return a + b\n"
    prop_2 = "def add(a, b):\n    # Robust add with type checks\n    assert isinstance(a, int)\n    return a + b\n"

        resource_id="math_util.py",

        proposals={"agent_be_1": prop_1, "agent_be_2": prop_2},
    )
    assert conflict is not None
    assert conflict.conflict_type == ConflictType.MERGE
    assert conflict.resolved is False

    # Resolve with CHOOSE_BEST
    resolved = resolver.resolve_conflict(conflict, preferred_action=ResolutionAction.CHOOSE_BEST)
    assert resolved.resolved is True
    assert resolved.winning_agent_id in ("agent_be_1", "agent_be_2")
    assert resolver.resolved_count == 1

"""
test_conflict_resolver.py - AutoDev Version 3.4
Unit and integration tests for Conflict Resolution Engine:

- Automated resolution via security authority, precedence, and diff synthesis

@pytest.fixture

def test_register_conflict(resolver: ConflictResolver):

def test_resolve_ownership_conflict_by_authority(resolver: ConflictResolver):

def test_resolve_merge_conflict_non_overlapping(resolver: ConflictResolver):
    base_code = "def start():\n    return True\n"
    prop_a = "def start():\n    return True\ndef feature_a():\n    return 'A'\n"
    prop_b = "def start():\n    return True\ndef feature_b():\n    return 'B'\n"

    rec = resolver.register_conflict(

"""
Tests for ConsensusEngine and review ratification in AutoDev v3.3.
"""

import pytest
from core.multi_agent.agent_registry import AgentRole
from core.multi_agent.consensus_engine import (
    ConsensusEngine,
    ConsensusProposal,
    ConsensusStrategy,
    ReviewVote,
    VoteDecision,
)


def test_majority_consensus_strategy():
    engine = ConsensusEngine()
    prop = engine.create_proposal(
        proposal_id="pr_1",
        title="Refactor Auth",
        description="Switch to OAuth2",
        strategy=ConsensusStrategy.MAJORITY,
    )

    engine.cast_vote(
        "pr_1",
        ReviewVote("dev_1", AgentRole.BACKEND_ENGINEER, VoteDecision.APPROVE),
    )
    engine.cast_vote(
        "pr_1",
        ReviewVote("dev_2", AgentRole.FRONTEND_ENGINEER, VoteDecision.APPROVE),
    )
    engine.cast_vote(
        "pr_1",
        ReviewVote("dev_3", AgentRole.QA_ENGINEER, VoteDecision.REJECT),
    )

    approved, reason, metrics = engine.evaluate_consensus("pr_1")
    assert approved is True
    assert metrics["approvals_count"] == 2
    assert metrics["rejections_count"] == 1
    assert prop.status == "APPROVED"


def test_weighted_majority_consensus_strategy():
    engine = ConsensusEngine()
    prop = engine.create_proposal(
        proposal_id="pr_2",
        title="Deploy to Prod",
        description="Production release candidate",
        strategy=ConsensusStrategy.WEIGHTED_MAJORITY,
    )

    # Chief Architect (weight 3.0) approves
    engine.cast_vote(
        "pr_2",
        ReviewVote("arch_1", AgentRole.CHIEF_ARCHITECT, VoteDecision.APPROVE),
    )
    # Two junior engineers (weight 1.0 each = 2.0 total) reject
    engine.cast_vote(
        "pr_2",
        ReviewVote("dev_1", AgentRole.BACKEND_ENGINEER, VoteDecision.REJECT),
    )
    engine.cast_vote(
        "pr_2",
        ReviewVote("dev_2", AgentRole.FRONTEND_ENGINEER, VoteDecision.REJECT),
    )

    approved, reason, metrics = engine.evaluate_consensus("pr_2")
    # Architect's 3.0 outweighs 2.0
    assert approved is True
    assert metrics["approve_weight"] == 3.0
    assert metrics["reject_weight"] == 2.0


def test_architect_override_strategy():
    engine = ConsensusEngine()
    prop = engine.create_proposal(
        proposal_id="pr_3",
        title="Change Tech Stack",
        description="Adopt Elixir",
        strategy=ConsensusStrategy.ARCHITECT_OVERRIDE,
    )

    # 4 developers approve
    for i in range(4):
        engine.cast_vote(
            "pr_3",
            ReviewVote(f"dev_{i}", AgentRole.BACKEND_ENGINEER, VoteDecision.APPROVE),
        )

    # Architect rejects
    engine.cast_vote(
        "pr_3",
        ReviewVote("arch_1", AgentRole.CHIEF_ARCHITECT, VoteDecision.REJECT),
    )

    approved, reason, metrics = engine.evaluate_consensus("pr_3")
    assert approved is False
    assert "Chief Architect arch_1 override: reject" in reason
    assert prop.status == "REJECTED"


def test_quality_and_confidence_threshold_strategies():
    engine = ConsensusEngine()

    # Quality threshold
    prop_q = engine.create_proposal(
        proposal_id="pr_q",
        title="Quality Gate",
        description="Verify quality metric",
        strategy=ConsensusStrategy.QUALITY_THRESHOLD,
        quality_threshold=85.0,
    )
    # Average quality 80.0 < 85.0
    engine.cast_vote(
        "pr_q",
        ReviewVote("qa_1", AgentRole.QA_ENGINEER, VoteDecision.APPROVE, quality_score=80.0),
    )
    approved, _, _ = engine.evaluate_consensus("pr_q")
    assert approved is False

    # Confidence threshold
    prop_c = engine.create_proposal(
        proposal_id="pr_c",
        title="Confidence Gate",
        description="Verify model confidence",
        strategy=ConsensusStrategy.CONFIDENCE_THRESHOLD,

"""
Unit and Integration Tests for High Availability Coordination, Consensus & Fencing (Phase 2 & Phase 8.1)
"""

import time
import pytest

from core.consensus_protocol import (
    CoordinatorRole,
    FencingToken,
    CoordinatorNode,
    VoteRequest,
    VoteResponse,
    ConsensusHeartbeat,
)
from core.ha_coordinator import (
    HACoordinator,
    LeaderFencingValidator,
    HAError,
    NotLeaderError,
    StaleLeaderError,
    FencingViolationError,
    QuorumLostError,
)
from core.coordination_store import MemoryCoordinationStore


class TestConsensusProtocolModels:
    def test_fencing_token_monotonic_and_expiry(self):
        token = FencingToken(term=1, leader_id="coord-1", fencing_generation=1, expires_at_timestamp=time.time() + 10.0)
        assert not token.is_expired
        assert token.is_valid_for(expected_term=1, expected_generation=1)
        assert not token.is_valid_for(expected_term=2, expected_generation=1)

        # Expired token
        expired_token = FencingToken(term=1, leader_id="coord-1", fencing_generation=1, expires_at_timestamp=time.time() - 1.0)
        assert expired_token.is_expired
        assert not expired_token.is_valid_for(expected_term=1, expected_generation=1)

    def test_fencing_token_serialization(self):
        token = FencingToken(term=3, leader_id="coord-alpha", fencing_generation=7)
        data = token.to_dict()
        assert data["term"] == 3
        assert data["leader_id"] == "coord-alpha"
        assert data["fencing_generation"] == 7

        recovered = FencingToken.from_dict(data)
        assert recovered.term == 3
        assert recovered.leader_id == "coord-alpha"
        assert recovered.fencing_generation == 7

    def test_coordinator_node_liveness(self):
        node = CoordinatorNode(coordinator_id="node-1", role=CoordinatorRole.FOLLOWER, last_heartbeat_timestamp=time.time())
        assert node.is_alive
        node.last_heartbeat_timestamp = time.time() - 20.0
        assert not node.is_alive

    def test_coordinator_node_serialization(self):
        node = CoordinatorNode(coordinator_id="node-xyz", role=CoordinatorRole.LEADER, current_term=4)
        d = node.to_dict()
        assert d["coordinator_id"] == "node-xyz"
        assert d["role"] == "LEADER"
        assert d["current_term"] == 4


class TestHACoordinatorElectionAndFencing:
    def test_single_coordinator_self_election(self):
        store = MemoryCoordinationStore()
        coord = HACoordinator(coordinator_id="coord-1", peer_ids=["coord-1"], store=store)
        assert coord.role == CoordinatorRole.STARTING

        won = coord.start_election()
        assert won is True
        assert coord.role == CoordinatorRole.LEADER
        assert coord.is_leader is True
        assert coord.current_term == 1
        assert coord.leader_id == "coord-1"

        token = coord.fencing_token
        assert token is not None
        assert token.term == 1
        assert token.leader_id == "coord-1"

    def test_three_node_cluster_election_quorum(self):
        store = MemoryCoordinationStore()
        peers = ["node-1", "node-2", "node-3"]
        c1 = HACoordinator(coordinator_id="node-1", peer_ids=peers, store=store)
        c2 = HACoordinator(coordinator_id="node-2", peer_ids=peers, store=store)
        c3 = HACoordinator(coordinator_id="node-3", peer_ids=peers, store=store)

        # Node 1 starts election
        req = VoteRequest(term=1, candidate_id="node-1", last_log_index=0, last_log_term=0)
        resp2 = c2.receive_vote_request(req)
        resp3 = c3.receive_vote_request(req)

        assert resp2.vote_granted is True
        assert resp3.vote_granted is True

        # Candidate node 1 becomes leader
        c1.role = CoordinatorRole.LEADER
        c1.current_term = 1
        c1.leader_id = "node-1"
        c1.current_generation += 1
        c1.fencing_token = FencingToken(term=1, leader_id="node-1", fencing_generation=c1.current_generation)

        # Node 1 sends heartbeat to followers
        hb = ConsensusHeartbeat(term=1, leader_id="node-1", fencing_generation=c1.current_generation)
        hb_resp2 = c2.receive_heartbeat(hb)
        hb_resp3 = c3.receive_heartbeat(hb)

        assert hb_resp2["success"] is True
        assert hb_resp3["success"] is True
        assert c2.leader_id == "node-1"
        assert c3.leader_id == "node-1"
        assert c2.role == CoordinatorRole.FOLLOWER
        assert c3.role == CoordinatorRole.FOLLOWER

    def test_candidate_rejects_lower_term_vote(self):
        store = MemoryCoordinationStore()
        c = HACoordinator(coordinator_id="node-1", peer_ids=["node-1", "node-2"], store=store)
        c.current_term = 5
        req = VoteRequest(term=4, candidate_id="node-2", last_log_index=0, last_log_term=0)
        resp = c.receive_vote_request(req)
        assert resp.vote_granted is False
        assert resp.term == 5

    def test_candidate_rejects_duplicate_vote_in_same_term(self):
        store = MemoryCoordinationStore()
        c = HACoordinator(coordinator_id="node-voter", peer_ids=["node-voter", "c1", "c2"], store=store)
        c.current_term = 2
        # First candidate gets vote
        req1 = VoteRequest(term=2, candidate_id="c1")
        resp1 = c.receive_vote_request(req1)
        assert resp1.vote_granted is True

        # Second candidate in same term is rejected
        req2 = VoteRequest(term=2, candidate_id="c2")
        resp2 = c.receive_vote_request(req2)
        assert resp2.vote_granted is False

    def test_peer_registration_and_deregistration(self):
        coord = HACoordinator(coordinator_id="master-node")
        assert coord.total_cluster_size == 1
        assert coord.quorum_size == 1

        peer = CoordinatorNode(coordinator_id="worker-node-1")
        coord.register_peer(peer)
        assert coord.total_cluster_size == 2
        assert coord.quorum_size == 2

        coord.deregister_peer("worker-node-1")
        assert coord.total_cluster_size == 1

    def test_role_change_callback_triggered(self):
        coord = HACoordinator(coordinator_id="cb-node")
        observed_roles = []
        coord.on_role_change(lambda role: observed_roles.append(role))

        coord.start_election()
        assert CoordinatorRole.CANDIDATE in observed_roles
        assert CoordinatorRole.LEADER in observed_roles

    def test_leader_lease_renewal(self):
        coord = HACoordinator(coordinator_id="renew-node", lease_duration_seconds=5.0)
        coord.start_election()
        assert coord.is_leader is True
        orig_expiry = coord.fencing_token.expires_at_timestamp

        time.sleep(0.1)
        renewed = coord.renew_leader_lease()
        assert renewed is True
        assert coord.fencing_token.expires_at_timestamp > orig_expiry

    def test_leader_fencing_validator_protects_mutations(self):
        store = MemoryCoordinationStore()
        c = HACoordinator(coordinator_id="node-1", peer_ids=["node-1"], store=store)
        validator = LeaderFencingValidator(c)

        # Should fail closed when not leader
        with pytest.raises(NotLeaderError):
            validator.assert_active_leader()

        # Elect leader
        c.start_election()
        # Now passes
        token = validator.assert_active_leader()
        assert token.term == 1

        # Step down
        c.step_down(reason="Stepping down for test")
        with pytest.raises(NotLeaderError):
            validator.assert_active_leader()

    def test_stale_leader_fencing_token_rejection(self):
        store = MemoryCoordinationStore()
        c = HACoordinator(coordinator_id="node-1", peer_ids=["node-1"], store=store)
        c.start_election()

        token1 = c.fencing_token
        validator = LeaderFencingValidator(c)

        # Token 1 is initially valid
        assert validator.validate_fencing_token(token1, minimum_generation=1) is True

        # Expired token is rejected
        expired_token = FencingToken(term=1, leader_id="node-1", fencing_generation=1, expires_at_timestamp=time.time() - 1.0)
        assert validator.validate_fencing_token(expired_token) is False

        # Higher generation requirement rejects outdated token
        assert validator.validate_fencing_token(token1, minimum_generation=999) is False

    def test_failover_reconciliation_safely_adopts_state(self):
        store = MemoryCoordinationStore()
        # Simulate previous leader registering state in durable store
        store.save_coordinator("old-leader", {"coordinator_id": "old-leader", "role": "LEADER", "current_term": 1})
        store.save_leadership(1, "old-leader", 1, time.time() + 10.0)

        # New coordinator elected in term 2
        new_coord = HACoordinator(coordinator_id="new-leader", peer_ids=["new-leader"], store=store)
        new_coord.start_election()
        assert new_coord.current_term == 1

        # Run failover reconciliation
        summary = new_coord.reconcile_failover()
        assert summary["status"] == "reconciled"
        assert summary["reconciled_by"] == "new-leader"

"""
Tests for consensus partition recovery, quorum loss fail-closed behavior, and transaction adoption.
"""

import time
import pytest
from core.consensus_provider import (
    MemoryConsensusProvider,
    LeadershipLease,
    LeadershipToken,
    QuorumUnavailableError,
    LeadershipLostError,
)
from core.ha_coordinator import HACoordinator, LeaderFencingValidator


def test_consensus_partition_and_recovery_flow():
    provider = MemoryConsensusProvider()
    coord1 = HACoordinator("coord-1", consensus_provider=provider, lease_duration_seconds=5.0)
    coord1.start()
    assert coord1.is_leader is True
    t1 = coord1.fencing_token
    assert t1 is not None

    # Simulate network partition
    provider.set_partitioned(True)

    # Protected mutation during partition must fail closed
    with pytest.raises(QuorumUnavailableError):
        provider.conditional_put("state_key", "value_1", expected_version=0, fencing_token=provider.get_fencing_token())

    # Heal network partition
    provider.set_partitioned(False)

    # After recovery, leadership can be renewed and writes succeed
    assert coord1.renew_leader_lease() is True
    token_recovered = provider.get_fencing_token()
    assert provider.conditional_put("state_key", "value_1", expected_version=0, fencing_token=token_recovered) is True

    coord1.stop()


def test_consensus_failover_reconciliation_with_in_flight_transactions():
    provider = MemoryConsensusProvider()
    coord_primary = HACoordinator("coord-primary", consensus_provider=provider, lease_duration_seconds=5.0)
    coord_primary.start()

    # Create mock transaction and lease manager
    class MockTx:
        def __init__(self, tx_id):
            self.transaction_id = tx_id
            self.status = "STAGE_RUNNING"

    class MockLeaseManager:
        def prune_expired_leases(self):
            return ["lease_orphaned_1", "lease_orphaned_2"]

    class MockJournal:
        def __init__(self):
            self.events = []
        def append_event(self, event_type, transaction_id, payload):
            self.events.append((event_type, transaction_id, payload))

    journal = MockJournal()
    tx1 = MockTx("tx-in-flight-1")
    tx2 = MockTx("tx-in-flight-2")

    report = coord_primary.reconcile_failover(
        active_transactions=[tx1, tx2],
        lease_manager=MockLeaseManager(),
        journal=journal,
    )

    assert report["status"] == "reconciled"
    assert report["reconciled_transactions"] == 2
    assert report["orphaned_leases_revoked"] == 2
    assert len(journal.events) == 2
    assert journal.events[0][0] == "ha.transaction_adopted"

    coord_primary.stop()

"""
Unit and Contract tests for AutoDev v2.5 ConsensusProvider interface and MemoryConsensusProvider.
"""

import time
import pytest
from core.consensus_provider import (

def test_consensus_provider_single_leader_election():
    provider = MemoryConsensusProvider()
    lease = provider.acquire_leadership("coord-1", term=1, ttl_seconds=5.0)

    assert lease.leader_id == "coord-1"
    assert lease.term == 1
    assert lease.generation == 1
    assert lease.is_active is True
    assert lease.is_expired is False
    assert provider.verify_leadership(lease) is True

    # Second coordinator attempting to acquire same term must be rejected
    with pytest.raises(LeadershipLostError):
        provider.acquire_leadership("coord-2", term=1, ttl_seconds=5.0)


def test_consensus_provider_lease_renewal():
    provider = MemoryConsensusProvider()
    lease = provider.acquire_leadership("coord-1", term=1, ttl_seconds=1.0)
    original_gen = lease.generation

    time.sleep(0.05)
    renewed = provider.renew_leadership(lease, ttl_seconds=2.0)

    assert renewed.leader_id == "coord-1"
    assert renewed.term == 1
    assert renewed.generation > original_gen
    assert renewed.expires_at > lease.expires_at
    assert provider.verify_leadership(renewed) is True


def test_consensus_provider_fencing_token_monotonic():
    provider = MemoryConsensusProvider()
    lease1 = provider.acquire_leadership("coord-1", term=1, ttl_seconds=5.0)
    token1 = provider.get_fencing_token()

    assert token1.leader_id == "coord-1"
    assert token1.term == 1
    assert token1.generation == 1

    # Release and elect coord-2 in term 2
    provider.release_leadership(lease1)
    lease2 = provider.acquire_leadership("coord-2", term=2, ttl_seconds=5.0)
    token2 = provider.get_fencing_token()

    assert token2.is_newer_than(token1) is True
    assert token1.is_stale_compared_to(token2.term, token2.generation) is True


def test_consensus_provider_conditional_put_and_delete():
    provider = MemoryConsensusProvider()
    lease = provider.acquire_leadership("coord-1", term=1, ttl_seconds=5.0)
    token = lease.fencing_token

    # Initial write with expected_version=0
    assert provider.conditional_put("key1", "val1", expected_version=0, fencing_token=token) is True
    val, ver = provider.get("key1")
    assert val == "val1"
    assert ver == 1

    # Conflict on outdated expected_version
    assert provider.conditional_put("key1", "val2", expected_version=0, fencing_token=token) is False

    # Successful update with correct expected_version=1
    assert provider.conditional_put("key1", "val2", expected_version=1, fencing_token=token) is True
    val2, ver2 = provider.get("key1")
    assert val2 == "val2"
    assert ver2 == 2

    # Conditional delete
    assert provider.conditional_delete("key1", expected_version=2, fencing_token=token) is True
    assert provider.get("key1") is None


def test_consensus_provider_stale_fencing_token_rejected():
    provider = MemoryConsensusProvider()
    lease = provider.acquire_leadership("coord-1", term=1, ttl_seconds=5.0)
    stale_token = LeadershipToken(leader_id="coord-1", term=0, generation=0)

    with pytest.raises(FencingTokenRejectedError):
        provider.conditional_put("key_fenced", "value", expected_version=0, fencing_token=stale_token)


def test_consensus_provider_network_partition_simulation():
    provider = MemoryConsensusProvider()
    provider.acquire_leadership("coord-1", term=1, ttl_seconds=5.0)

    # Inject network partition
    provider.set_partitioned(True)

    with pytest.raises(QuorumUnavailableError):
        provider.get("some_key")

    with pytest.raises(QuorumUnavailableError):
        provider.conditional_put("key", "val")

    health = provider.get_health()
    assert health.is_healthy is False

    # Heal partition
    provider.set_partitioned(False)
    assert provider.get_health().is_healthy is True
