"""
test_enterprise_scenarios.py - Real-World Corporate Operational Scenarios (v3.0)
"""

import pytest
from core.enterprise import (
    ArchitectureBoard,
    ArchitectureScorecard,
    BusinessAnalytics,
    CompanyBrain,
    ComplianceStandard,
    DecisionStatus,
    DepartmentType,
    EngineeringManager,
    EnterpriseCompany,
    ExecutiveDecisionEngine,
    ExecutiveRole,
    ExpenseCategory,
    FinanceManager,
    GovernanceManager,
    HiringManager,
    KnowledgeCategory,
    OrganizationGraph,
    PriorityLevel,
    ProductFeature,
    ProductManager,
    ReleaseCandidate,
    ReleaseStage,
    ReleaseTrain,
    SprintManager,
    SupportCenter,
    SupportTicket,
    TeamType,
    TicketPriority,
    TicketType,
    UserStory,
)


class TestEnterpriseScenarios:
    def test_emergency_security_hotfix_scenario(self):
        """
        Scenario: A critical CVE is discovered in the authentication token parser.
        Workflow:
        1. Support Center receives P0_CRITICAL ticket
        2. Auto-converts to Security Ops engineering task
        3. Security Director proposes emergency hotfix decision
        4. Architecture Board evaluates security scorecard
        5. Release Train creates HOTFIX candidate, passes gates, gathers CTO/CSO signoffs, and deploys.
        """
        company = EnterpriseCompany()

        # 1. Ingest P0 ticket
        ticket = company.support_center.submit_ticket(
            customer_id="enterprise_sec_team",
            ticket_type=TicketType.INCIDENT,
            priority=TicketPriority.P0_CRITICAL,
            title="CVE-2026-999: Auth Token Buffer Overrun",
            description="Buffer overrun in ECDSA signature parser requires immediate patch.",
            assigned_team=TeamType.SECURITY_OPS,
        )
        assert ticket.status == "IN_ENGINEERING"
        assert ticket.linked_engineering_task_id is not None

        # 2. Executive emergency decision
        dec = company.executive_engine.propose_decision(
            title="Authorize Emergency Hotfix Release 3.0.1",
            description="Immediate security deployment to patch CVE-2026-999",
            proposer_role=ExecutiveRole.DIRECTOR_SECURITY,
            required_signoffs=[ExecutiveRole.CTO, ExecutiveRole.DIRECTOR_SECURITY],
            risk_score=5.0,
        )
        company.executive_engine.signoff_decision(dec.decision_id, ExecutiveRole.CTO, approved=True)
        company.executive_engine.signoff_decision(dec.decision_id, ExecutiveRole.DIRECTOR_SECURITY, approved=True)

        # 3. Release Train hotfix
        hotfix_rc = company.release_train.create_release_candidate(
            target_version="3.0.1",
            stage=ReleaseStage.HOTFIX,
            bugs=["CVE-2026-999"],
        )
        company.release_train.set_gate_status(hotfix_rc.release_id, "security_scan_clean", True)
        company.release_train.signoff_release(hotfix_rc.release_id, ExecutiveRole.CTO)
        company.release_train.signoff_release(hotfix_rc.release_id, ExecutiveRole.DIRECTOR_SECURITY)

        deployed_hotfix = company.release_train.promote_to_general_availability(hotfix_rc.release_id)
        assert deployed_hotfix.version == "3.0.1"
        assert company.release_train.get_current_version() == "3.0.1"

        # 4. Resolve incident ticket
        company.support_center.resolve_ticket(
            ticket.ticket_id,
            resolution_notes="Hotfix 3.0.1 deployed to production cluster.",
            rca="Bounds checking flaw in signature parsing subroutine.",
            csat_score=5,
        )
        updated_ticket = company.support_center.get_ticket(ticket.ticket_id)
        assert updated_ticket.status == "RESOLVED"

    def test_quarterly_budget_burn_and_cost_optimization_scenario(self):
        """
        Scenario: High cloud and LLM spending threatens quarterly budget.
        Workflow:
        1. Record multiple operational expenses
        2. Finance Manager detects high cloud & LLM spend
        3. Generates automated cost optimization recommendations
        4. Director of Finance tracks ROI on optimization initiative.
        """
        finance = FinanceManager(initial_cash_reserve_usd=5000000.0)

        # Record heavy compute and LLM token expenses
        for m in range(3):
            finance.record_expense(ExpenseCategory.INFRASTRUCTURE_CLOUD, 80000.0, f"Month {m+1} Cloud", DepartmentType.DEVOPS)
            finance.record_expense(ExpenseCategory.LLM_API_TOKENS, 40000.0, f"Month {m+1} Tokens", DepartmentType.ENGINEERING)

        recs = finance.generate_cost_optimization_recommendations()
        assert len(recs) >= 2
        categories = [r["category"] for r in recs]
        assert ExpenseCategory.INFRASTRUCTURE_CLOUD.value in categories

        # Calculate ROI of optimization initiative (invest $10k in spot node automation, save $60k/quarter)
        roi = finance.calculate_roi(invested_cost_usd=10000.0, expected_revenue_or_savings_usd=60000.0)
        assert roi == 500.0

    def test_postmortem_and_institutional_knowledge_scenario(self):
        """
        Scenario: Production incident resolution generates an ADR and Postmortem in Company Brain.
        Workflow:
        1. Store postmortem in CompanyBrain
        2. Store updated architectural ADR
        3. Link ADR and Postmortem bidirectionally
        4. Verify cross-searchability.
        """
        brain = CompanyBrain()

        postmortem = brain.store_knowledge(
            title="Postmortem: High Memory Pressure on Master Node",
            category=KnowledgeCategory.POSTMORTEM,
            content="Task queue grew excessively due to slow worker heartbeats. Resolution: implemented task queue backpressure.",
            tags=["postmortem", "memory", "master_node", "backpressure"],
            author="Rachel Green (DevOps)",
            department=DepartmentType.DEVOPS,
        )

        adr = brain.store_knowledge(
            title="ADR-004: Adaptive Queue Backpressure & Rate Limiting",
            category=KnowledgeCategory.ARCHITECTURE_ADR,
            content="Master node rejects task submissions when memory exceeds 85% threshold.",
            tags=["adr", "architecture", "backpressure", "rate_limiting"],
            author="Marcus Vance (CTO)",
            department=DepartmentType.ARCHITECTURE,
        )

        brain.link_knowledge(postmortem.knowledge_id, adr.knowledge_id)

        related_to_pm = brain.get_related_knowledge(postmortem.knowledge_id)
        assert len(related_to_pm) == 1
        assert related_to_pm[0].title == adr.title

        related_to_adr = brain.get_related_knowledge(adr.knowledge_id)
        assert len(related_to_adr) == 1
        assert related_to_adr[0].title == postmortem.title

"""
test_enterprise_security.py - Unit Tests for EnterpriseSecurityManager (AutoDev Version 3.5)
"""

import time
import pytest

from core.enterprise_security import (
    EnterpriseCertificate,
    EnterpriseSecurityManager,
    FederatedIdentity,
    SecurityAuditEntry,
)


def test_security_manager_initialization():
    sec = EnterpriseSecurityManager(master_secret="TEST_ROOT_SECRET")
    dash = sec.get_security_dashboard()
    assert dash["active_identities_count"] == 0
    assert dash["stored_secrets_count"] == 0
    assert dash["audit_chain_valid"] is True


def test_federated_identity_and_token():
    sec = EnterpriseSecurityManager()
    ident = sec.create_identity(
        company_id="COMP-A",
        department_id="SECURITY",
        role_name="SecEngineer",
        clearance_level="CONFIDENTIAL",
        permissions=["read:audit", "write:firewall"],
    )
    assert ident.identity_id.startswith("ID-")
    assert ident.token is not None
    assert ident.has_permission("read:audit") is True
    assert ident.has_permission("admin:root") is False

    validated = sec.validate_token(ident.token)
    assert validated is not None
    assert validated.identity_id == ident.identity_id


def test_token_revocation():
    sec = EnterpriseSecurityManager()
    ident = sec.create_identity("COMP-A", "ENG", "Dev")
    assert sec.validate_token(ident.token) is not None

    assert sec.revoke_token(ident.token, reason="Compromised session") is True
    assert sec.validate_token(ident.token) is None


def test_zero_trust_authorization_success():
    sec = EnterpriseSecurityManager()
    ident = sec.create_identity(
        company_id="COMP-A",
        department_id="ENG",
        role_name="Architect",
        clearance_level="CONFIDENTIAL",
        permissions=["deploy:staging"],
    )
    ok, reason = sec.authorize_action(
        token=ident.token,
        target_company_id="COMP-B",
        required_permission="deploy:staging",
        resource_clearance="INTERNAL",
    )
    assert ok is True
    assert reason == "Authorized"


def test_zero_trust_authorization_insufficient_clearance():
    sec = EnterpriseSecurityManager()
    ident = sec.create_identity(
        company_id="COMP-A",
        department_id="ENG",
        role_name="Intern",
        clearance_level="INTERNAL",
        permissions=["read:all"],
    )
    ok, reason = sec.authorize_action(
        token=ident.token,
        target_company_id="COMP-B",
        required_permission="read:all",
        resource_clearance="RESTRICTED",  # Higher than INTERNAL
    )
    assert ok is False
    assert "Clearance insufficient" in reason


def test_zero_trust_authorization_missing_permission():
    sec = EnterpriseSecurityManager()
    ident = sec.create_identity(
        company_id="COMP-A",
        department_id="ENG",
        role_name="Dev",
        clearance_level="CONFIDENTIAL",
        permissions=["read:logs"],
    )
    ok, reason = sec.authorize_action(
        token=ident.token,
        target_company_id="COMP-B",
        required_permission="delete:database",
        resource_clearance="CONFIDENTIAL",
    )
    assert ok is False
    assert "Missing 'delete:database'" in reason


def test_certificate_issuance_and_verification():
    sec = EnterpriseSecurityManager()
    cert = sec.issue_certificate("COMP-A", validity_days=30)
    assert cert.cert_id.startswith("CERT-")
    assert cert.subject_company == "COMP-A"
    assert sec.verify_certificate(cert.cert_id) is True

    # Revoke certificate
    assert sec.revoke_certificate(cert.cert_id, reason="Certificate renewal") is True
    assert sec.verify_certificate(cert.cert_id) is False


def test_secrets_vault_encryption_and_retrieval():
    sec = EnterpriseSecurityManager()
    ident = sec.create_identity("COMP-A", "ENG", "Dev", clearance_level="CONFIDENTIAL", permissions=["secrets:read"])

    assert sec.store_secret("DB_PROD_PASSWORD", "SuperSecurePass_2026!", "COMP-A", "CONFIDENTIAL") is True

    # Authorized retrieval
    retrieved = sec.retrieve_secret("DB_PROD_PASSWORD", ident.token)
    assert retrieved == "SuperSecurePass_2026!"

    # Unauthorized retrieval (low clearance)
    ident_low = sec.create_identity("COMP-B", "ENG", "Junior", clearance_level="PUBLIC", permissions=["secrets:read"])
    assert sec.retrieve_secret("DB_PROD_PASSWORD", ident_low.token) is None


def test_threat_propagation_and_quarantine():
    sec = EnterpriseSecurityManager()
    ident_a = sec.create_identity("COMP-MALICIOUS", "CORE", "AgentA")
    ident_b = sec.create_identity("COMP-SAFE", "CORE", "AgentB")

    # Propagate threat
    event = sec.propagate_threat(
        compromised_company_id="COMP-MALICIOUS",
        threat_type="EXFILTRATION_ACTIVITY",
        indicators_of_compromise=["192.168.1.100", "payload.bin"],
    )
    assert event["action_taken"] == "QUARANTINE_COMPANY"
    assert event["revoked_tokens_count"] == 1

    # Malicious company identity should now be rejected
    assert sec.validate_token(ident_a.token) is None

    # Safe company identity should still be valid
    assert sec.validate_token(ident_b.token) is not None

    # Lift quarantine
    assert sec.lift_quarantine("COMP-MALICIOUS") is True


def test_cryptographic_audit_chain_tamper_evidence():
    sec = EnterpriseSecurityManager()
    for i in range(5):
        sec.create_identity("COMP-A", "DEPT", f"Role{i}")

    assert sec.verify_audit_chain_integrity() is True

    # Simulate adversarial tampering with block 2
    sec._audit_chain[2].actor = "ADVERSARY_HACKER"
    # Tampered block must fail cryptographic verification
    assert sec.verify_audit_chain_integrity() is False

"""
test_enterprise_stress.py - High-Scale Stress & Scalability Tests for Enterprise Subsystems (v3.0)
"""

import time
import pytest
from core.enterprise import (
    BusinessAnalytics,
    CompanyBrain,
    CompanySimulator,
    DepartmentType,
    EngineeringManager,
    EnterpriseCompany,
    ExecutiveDecisionEngine,
    ExecutiveRole,
    ExpenseCategory,
    FinanceManager,
    GovernanceManager,
    HiringManager,
    KnowledgeCategory,
    OrganizationGraph,
    OrgNode,
    EdgeRelation,
    ProductManager,
    ReleaseStage,
    ReleaseTrain,
    SprintManager,
    SupportCenter,
    TeamType,
    TicketPriority,
    TicketType,
    UserStory,
)


class TestEnterpriseStressAndScalability:
    def test_high_volume_executive_decisions(self):
        engine = ExecutiveDecisionEngine()
        start = time.time()
        for i in range(250):
            dec = engine.propose_decision(
                title=f"Decision Proposal #{i}",
                description=f"Automated stress test proposal #{i}",
                proposer_role=ExecutiveRole.VP_ENGINEERING,
                required_signoffs=[ExecutiveRole.CTO, ExecutiveRole.DIRECTOR_FINANCE],
                budget_impact_usd=1000.0 * (i + 1),
            )
            engine.signoff_decision(dec.decision_id, ExecutiveRole.CTO, approved=True)
            engine.signoff_decision(dec.decision_id, ExecutiveRole.DIRECTOR_FINANCE, approved=True)

        duration = time.time() - start
        assert len(engine.list_decisions()) == 250
        assert duration < 5.0

    def test_massive_support_ticket_ingestion_and_routing(self):
        support = SupportCenter()
        start = time.time()
        for i in range(500):
            priority = TicketPriority.P0_CRITICAL if i % 20 == 0 else TicketPriority.P2_MEDIUM
            t_type = TicketType.BUG_REPORT if i % 2 == 0 else TicketType.INQUIRY
            support.submit_ticket(
                customer_id=f"cust_stress_{i}",
                ticket_type=t_type,
                priority=priority,
                title=f"Stress incident ticket {i} with database queries",
                description=f"Detailed failure logs for test #{i}",
            )

        duration = time.time() - start
        metrics = support.get_metrics()
        assert metrics["total_tickets"] == 500
        assert metrics["p0_critical_tickets"] == 25
        assert duration < 5.0

    def test_deep_organization_graph_traversal(self):
        org = OrganizationGraph()
        # Build a deep hierarchy of 100 levels
        prev_node = "emp_vpeng"
        for i in range(100):
            nid = f"emp_deep_{i}"
            org.add_node(OrgNode(nid, f"Engineer {i}", f"L{i} Specialist", DepartmentType.ENGINEERING))
            org.add_edge(nid, prev_node, EdgeRelation.REPORTS_TO)
            prev_node = nid

        path = org.find_escalation_path(f"emp_deep_99", "emp_ceo")
        assert len(path) > 100
        assert path[0] == "emp_deep_99"
        assert path[-1] == "emp_ceo"

    def test_cryptographic_audit_trail_chain_1000_records(self):
        gov = GovernanceManager()
        start = time.time()
        for i in range(1000):
            gov.log_audit_event(
                action="STRESS_TRANSACTION",
                actor=f"Agent-{i % 10}",
                target_entity=f"Entity-{i}",
                department=DepartmentType.ENGINEERING,
                details={"index": i, "data": f"payload-{i}"},
            )

        duration = time.time() - start
        valid, error = gov.verify_audit_trail_integrity()
        assert valid is True
        assert error is None
        assert duration < 5.0

    def test_high_volume_knowledge_indexing_and_search(self):
        brain = CompanyBrain()
        start = time.time()
        for i in range(300):
            cat = KnowledgeCategory.ARCHITECTURE_ADR if i % 2 == 0 else KnowledgeCategory.POSTMORTEM
            brain.store_knowledge(
                title=f"Architecture Document #{i} for Cluster Scaling",
                category=cat,
                content=f"Detailed specifications and benchmarks for high-throughput node #{i}.",
                tags=["stress", f"tag_{i%10}", "cluster", "performance"],
                author=f"Architect #{i%5}",
                department=DepartmentType.ENGINEERING,
            )

        duration = time.time() - start
        res = brain.search_knowledge(query="Cluster Scaling", limit=50)
        assert len(res) == 50
        assert duration < 5.0

    def test_multi_year_simulation_stress(self):
        company = EnterpriseCompany()
        start = time.time()
        
        # Simulate 2 full operating years
        y1 = company.simulator.simulate_year(2026)
        y2 = company.simulator.simulate_year(2027)

        duration = time.time() - start

"""
Unit and Integration tests for etcd v3 and Consul external consensus adapters.
"""

import pytest
from core.consensus_provider import (
    ConsensusConfiguration,
    ConsensusConfigurationError,
    FencingTokenRejectedError,
    LeadershipLostError,
    LeadershipToken,
    QuorumUnavailableError,
)
from core.etcd_consensus_adapter import EtcdConsensusAdapter
from core.consul_consensus_adapter import ConsulConsensusAdapter


def test_etcd_adapter_config_validation():
    # Empty endpoints
    with pytest.raises(ConsensusConfigurationError):
        EtcdConsensusAdapter(ConsensusConfiguration(endpoints=[]))

    # Invalid timeout
    with pytest.raises(ConsensusConfigurationError):
        EtcdConsensusAdapter(ConsensusConfiguration(timeout_seconds=0))


def test_etcd_adapter_lifecycle_and_fencing():
    config = ConsensusConfiguration(
        provider_type="etcd",
        endpoints=["127.0.0.1:2379"],
        prefix="/autodev/test",
        lease_ttl_seconds=5.0,
    )
    adapter = EtcdConsensusAdapter(config)

    lease = adapter.acquire_leadership("coordinator-etcd-1", term=1, ttl_seconds=5.0)
    assert lease.leader_id == "coordinator-etcd-1"
    assert lease.term == 1
    assert adapter.verify_leadership(lease) is True

    # Renew lease
    renewed = adapter.renew_leadership(lease, ttl_seconds=5.0)
    assert renewed.generation > lease.generation
    assert adapter.verify_leadership(renewed) is True

    # Conditional write with valid fencing token
    token = adapter.get_fencing_token()
    assert adapter.conditional_put("/autodev/test/state", "ok", expected_version=0, fencing_token=token) is True

    # Stale token write must be rejected
    stale = LeadershipToken(leader_id="coordinator-etcd-1", term=0, generation=0)
    with pytest.raises(FencingTokenRejectedError):
        adapter.conditional_put("/autodev/test/state", "bad", expected_version=1, fencing_token=stale)

    # Simulated partition fails closed
    adapter.set_partitioned(True)
    with pytest.raises(QuorumUnavailableError):
        adapter.acquire_leadership("coordinator-etcd-2", term=2)

    adapter.set_partitioned(False)
    adapter.release_leadership(renewed)
    adapter.close()


def test_consul_adapter_lifecycle_and_fencing():
    config = ConsensusConfiguration(
        provider_type="consul",
        endpoints=["127.0.0.1:8500"],
        prefix="autodev/consul_test",
        lease_ttl_seconds=5.0,
    )
    adapter = ConsulConsensusAdapter(config)

    lease = adapter.acquire_leadership("coordinator-consul-1", term=1, ttl_seconds=5.0)
    assert lease.leader_id == "coordinator-consul-1"
    assert lease.term == 1
    assert adapter.verify_leadership(lease) is True

    # Renew lease
    renewed = adapter.renew_leadership(lease, ttl_seconds=5.0)
    assert renewed.generation > lease.generation
    assert adapter.verify_leadership(renewed) is True

    # Conditional write with valid token
    token = adapter.get_fencing_token()
    assert adapter.conditional_put("autodev/consul_test/key1", "val1", expected_version=0, fencing_token=token) is True

    # Stale token write rejected
    stale = LeadershipToken(leader_id="coordinator-consul-1", term=0, generation=0)
    with pytest.raises(FencingTokenRejectedError):
        adapter.conditional_put("autodev/consul_test/key1", "val2", expected_version=1, fencing_token=stale)

    # Release leadership
    adapter.release_leadership(renewed)
    adapter.close()

def test_blocking_validation_gate_failure_triggers_automatic_verified_rollback(tmp_path):
    """
    Verifies that when a blocking validation gate fails:
    1. Downstream stages are NOT scheduled.
    2. Automatic rollback restores the original workspace state.
    3. The restored state is 100% verified.
    """
    # Pre-existing file
    existing_file = tmp_path / "core" / "app.py"
    existing_file.parent.mkdir(parents=True)
    existing_file.write_text("APP_INITIAL_STATE = True\n", encoding="utf-8")

    op_modify = ChangeOperation(
        operation_id="OP-MOD-1",
        operation_type=OperationType.MODIFY_FILE.value,
        file="core/app.py",
        target_content="APP_INITIAL_STATE = False\nSYNTAX_ERROR_BROKEN ::::\n",
    )
    op_downstream = ChangeOperation(
        operation_id="OP-DOWNSTREAM-2",
        operation_type=OperationType.CREATE_FILE.value,
        file="core/downstream.py",
        target_content="# Should never be created\n",
    )

    # Stage 1 has a syntax error that will fail py_compile validation
    stage1 = ExecutionStage(
        stage_number=1,
        title="Failing Stage",
        operations=[op_modify],
        validation_gates=[
            ValidationGate(
                gate_id="gate-compile-fail",
                gate_type=GateType.COMPILE.value,
                command="python -m py_compile core/app.py",
                description="Syntax verification",
                blocking=True,
            )
        ],
    )
    stage2 = ExecutionStage(
        stage_number=2,
        title="Downstream Stage",
        operations=[op_downstream],
    )

    failing_plan = ChangeExecutionPlan(
        plan_id="CEP-FAIL-ROLLBACK",
        task_id="TASK-FAIL",
        ordered_stages=[stage1, stage2],
    )

    engine = ExecutionEngine(
        workspace_root=tmp_path,
        journal_root=tmp_path / "journal",
        report_dir=tmp_path / "reports",
    )

    report: ExecutionReport = engine.execute_plan(
        failing_plan, mode="apply", auto_rollback=True
    )

    # 1. Overall execution failed
    assert report.overall_success is False
    assert report.status in {ExecutionStatus.ROLLED_BACK, ExecutionStatus.FAILED}
    assert report.stages_failed == 1
    assert report.stages_completed == 0

    # 2. Downstream stage was NEVER executed
    assert not (tmp_path / "core" / "downstream.py").exists()

    # 3. Modified file was automatically restored to original content
    assert existing_file.read_text(encoding="utf-8") == "APP_INITIAL_STATE = True\n"
    assert report.rollback_summary is not None
    assert report.rollback_summary["verification_passed"] is True

"""
test_execution_journal.py - Comprehensive Tests for Durable Event Journaling & Crash Recovery (v2.1)
"""

import json
import pytest
from pathlib import Path

from core.execution_journal import (
    ExecutionJournal,
    JournalError,
    JournalEvent,
    JournalIntegrityError,
    redact_secrets,
)
from core.execution_transaction import ExecutionStatus, ExecutionTransaction


# =============================================================================
# 1. SECRET REDACTION TESTS
# =============================================================================

def test_redact_secrets_dictionary():
    """Verifies that sensitive keys and token formats are redacted."""
    raw_payload = {
        "api_key": "sk-1234567890abcdef1234567890",
        "user_password": "super_secret_password",
        "auth_token": "Bearer eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9",
        "safe_field": "database_table_users",
        "nested": {
            "secret_key": "AIzaSyD9876543210abcdefghijklmnopq",
            "normal": 42,
        },
    }
    redacted = redact_secrets(raw_payload)
    assert redacted["api_key"] == "[REDACTED]"
    assert redacted["user_password"] == "[REDACTED]"
    assert redacted["auth_token"] == "[REDACTED]"
    assert redacted["safe_field"] == "database_table_users"
    assert redacted["nested"]["secret_key"] == "[REDACTED]"
    assert redacted["nested"]["normal"] == 42


def test_redact_secrets_string_patterns():

    raw_str = "Authorization: Bearer sk-1234567890123456789012345 in header."
    clean = redact_secrets(raw_str)
    assert "sk-1234567890123456789012345" not in clean
    assert "[REDACTED]" in clean


# =============================================================================
# 2. EVENT HASH CHAINING TESTS
# =============================================================================

def test_journal_event_hash_chain():
    """Verifies that JournalEvent computes deterministic SHA256 checksums."""
    evt1 = JournalEvent(
        event_id="EVT-001",
        transaction_id="tx-01",
        seq_num=1,
        event_type="TRANSACTION_CREATED",
        payload={"task_id": "T1"},
        prev_hash="GENESIS",
    )
    evt1.seal()
    assert evt1.event_hash is not None
    assert len(evt1.event_hash) == 64

    evt2 = JournalEvent(
        event_id="EVT-002",
        transaction_id="tx-01",
        seq_num=2,
        event_type="STAGE_STARTED",
        payload={"stage": 1},
        prev_hash=evt1.event_hash,
    )
    evt2.seal()
    assert evt2.event_hash is not None
    assert evt2.prev_hash == evt1.event_hash


# =============================================================================
# 3. JOURNAL APPEND & PERSISTENCE TESTS
# =============================================================================

def test_execution_journal_append_and_load(tmp_path):
    """Verifies appending events to disk and loading them with integrity verification."""
    journal = ExecutionJournal(transaction_id="tx-append-01", journal_root=tmp_path)

    evt1 = journal.append_event("TRANSACTION_CREATED", {"task": "TASK-1"})
    evt2 = journal.append_event("LOCK_ACQUIRED", {"pid": 1234})
    evt3 = journal.append_event("STAGE_COMPLETED", {"stage_number": 1})

    assert journal.event_count == 3
    assert evt1.seq_num == 1
    assert evt2.seq_num == 2
    assert evt3.seq_num == 3

    # Load from disk with hash-chain verification
    loaded_journal = ExecutionJournal(transaction_id="tx-append-01", journal_root=tmp_path)
    loaded_events = loaded_journal.load_events(verify_integrity=True)

    assert len(loaded_events) == 3
    assert loaded_events[0].event_type == "TRANSACTION_CREATED"
    assert loaded_events[1].event_type == "LOCK_ACQUIRED"
    assert loaded_events[2].event_type == "STAGE_COMPLETED"
    assert loaded_events[1].prev_hash == loaded_events[0].event_hash
    assert loaded_events[2].prev_hash == loaded_events[1].event_hash


def test_execution_journal_integrity_detection_tampering(tmp_path):
    """Verifies that JournalIntegrityError is raised if an event line is modified or corrupted."""
    journal = ExecutionJournal(transaction_id="tx-tamper-01", journal_root=tmp_path)
    journal.append_event("EVENT_1", {"data": 100})
    journal.append_event("EVENT_2", {"data": 200})

    # Tamper with the events file on disk
    events_file = tmp_path / "tx-tamper-01" / "events.jsonl"
    lines = events_file.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines()
    # Modify payload of line 1 without updating hash
    tampered_data = json.loads(lines[0])
    tampered_data["payload"]["data"] = 999
    lines[0] = json.dumps(tampered_data)
    events_file.write_text("\n".join(lines) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")

    # Loading must detect hash mismatch
    verifier = ExecutionJournal(transaction_id="tx-tamper-01", journal_root=tmp_path)
    with pytest.raises(JournalIntegrityError) as exc_info:
        verifier.load_events(verify_integrity=True)
    assert "hash mismatch" in str(exc_info.value).lower() or "hash chain broken" in str(exc_info.value).lower()


def test_execution_journal_integrity_detection_sequence_gap(tmp_path):
    """Verifies that JournalIntegrityError is raised if an event is dropped."""
    journal = ExecutionJournal(transaction_id="tx-gap-01", journal_root=tmp_path)
    journal.append_event("EVENT_1", {})
    journal.append_event("EVENT_2", {})
    journal.append_event("EVENT_3", {})

    # Delete middle line
    events_file = tmp_path / "tx-gap-01" / "events.jsonl"
    lines = events_file.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines()
    del lines[1]
    events_file.write_text("\n".join(lines) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")

    verifier = ExecutionJournal(transaction_id="tx-gap-01", journal_root=tmp_path)
    with pytest.raises(JournalIntegrityError):
        verifier.load_events(verify_integrity=True)


# =============================================================================
# 4. TRANSACTION SNAPSHOT PERSISTENCE & DISCOVERY
# =============================================================================

def test_persist_and_load_transaction_snapshot(tmp_path):
    """Verifies atomic snapshot saving and loading of ExecutionTransaction."""
    journal = ExecutionJournal(transaction_id="tx-snap-01", journal_root=tmp_path)

    tx = ExecutionTransaction(
        transaction_id="tx-snap-01",
        plan_id="plan-99",
        task_id="task-99",
        workspace_root=tmp_path,
        initial_git_head="head-sha",
    )
    tx.record_change("core/app.py", "CREATE")
    tx.transition_to(ExecutionStatus.VALIDATING)
    tx.transition_to(ExecutionStatus.READY)
    tx.transition_to(ExecutionStatus.RUNNING)

    journal.persist_transaction_snapshot(tx)

    # Load back
    loaded_tx = journal.load_transaction_snapshot()
    assert loaded_tx is not None
    assert loaded_tx.transaction_id == "tx-snap-01"
    assert loaded_tx.status == ExecutionStatus.RUNNING
    assert "core/app.py" in loaded_tx.created_files


def test_discover_interrupted_transactions(tmp_path):
    """Verifies scanning for unfinished transactions across the journal root."""
    # 1. Active RUNNING transaction
    j1 = ExecutionJournal("tx-active-01", journal_root=tmp_path)
    t1 = ExecutionTransaction("tx-active-01", "p1", "t1", tmp_path)
    t1.transition_to(ExecutionStatus.VALIDATING)
    t1.transition_to(ExecutionStatus.READY)
    t1.transition_to(ExecutionStatus.RUNNING)
    j1.persist_transaction_snapshot(t1)

    # 2. Completed SUCCEEDED transaction
    j2 = ExecutionJournal("tx-done-02", journal_root=tmp_path)
    t2 = ExecutionTransaction("tx-done-02", "p2", "t2", tmp_path)
    t2.transition_to(ExecutionStatus.VALIDATING)
    t2.transition_to(ExecutionStatus.READY)
    t2.transition_to(ExecutionStatus.RUNNING)
    t2.transition_to(ExecutionStatus.SUCCEEDED)
    j2.persist_transaction_snapshot(t2)

    # 3. Interrupted ROLLING_BACK transaction
    j3 = ExecutionJournal("tx-recovering-03", journal_root=tmp_path)
    t3 = ExecutionTransaction("tx-recovering-03", "p3", "t3", tmp_path)
    t3.transition_to(ExecutionStatus.VALIDATING)
    t3.transition_to(ExecutionStatus.READY)
    t3.transition_to(ExecutionStatus.RUNNING)
    t3.transition_to(ExecutionStatus.ROLLING_BACK)
    j3.persist_transaction_snapshot(t3)

    interrupted = ExecutionJournal.discover_interrupted_transactions(journal_root=tmp_path)
    interrupted_ids = {item[0] for item in interrupted}

    assert "tx-active-01" in interrupted_ids
    assert "tx-recovering-03" in interrupted_ids
    assert "tx-done-02" not in interrupted_ids

"""
test_execution_lock.py - Comprehensive Tests for Workspace Locking & Concurrency Control (v2.1)
"""

import json
import os
import socket
import time
import pytest
from pathlib import Path

from core.execution_lock import (
    LockAcquisitionTimeoutError,
    LockMetadata,
    LockOwnershipError,
    ParallelOperationScheduler,
    WorkspaceLock,
    WorkspaceLockError,
)


# =============================================================================
# 1. WORKSPACE LOCK TESTS
# =============================================================================

def test_workspace_lock_acquire_and_release(tmp_path):
    """Verifies atomic acquisition and clean release of workspace lock."""
    lock = WorkspaceLock(workspace_root=tmp_path)
    assert lock.is_locked is False

    meta = lock.acquire(transaction_id="tx-lock-01", timeout_seconds=1.0)
    assert meta.transaction_id == "tx-lock-01"
    assert meta.pid == os.getpid()
    assert lock.is_locked is True
    assert (tmp_path / ".autodev.lock").exists()

    # Release
    released = lock.release(transaction_id="tx-lock-01")
    assert released is True
    assert lock.is_locked is False
    assert not (tmp_path / ".autodev.lock").exists()


def test_workspace_lock_reentrant_same_transaction(tmp_path):
    """Verifies that acquiring the lock twice with the same tx_id and PID succeeds."""
    lock = WorkspaceLock(workspace_root=tmp_path)
    meta1 = lock.acquire(transaction_id="tx-reenter-01", timeout_seconds=1.0)
    meta2 = lock.acquire(transaction_id="tx-reenter-01", timeout_seconds=1.0)

    assert meta1.owner_token == meta2.owner_token
    assert lock.is_locked is True
    lock.release(transaction_id="tx-reenter-01")


def test_workspace_lock_timeout_different_transaction(tmp_path):
    """Verifies that a competing transaction times out while waiting for the lock."""
    lock1 = WorkspaceLock(workspace_root=tmp_path)
    lock1.acquire(transaction_id="tx-first-01", timeout_seconds=1.0)

    lock2 = WorkspaceLock(workspace_root=tmp_path)
    with pytest.raises(LockAcquisitionTimeoutError) as exc_info:
        lock2.acquire(transaction_id="tx-competing-02", timeout_seconds=0.2)

    assert "Could not acquire workspace lock" in str(exc_info.value)
    lock1.release("tx-first-01")


def test_workspace_lock_release_ownership_verification(tmp_path):
    """Verifies that an unauthorized entity cannot release someone else's lock."""
    lock = WorkspaceLock(workspace_root=tmp_path)
    lock.acquire(transaction_id="tx-owner-01")

    with pytest.raises(LockOwnershipError) as exc_info:
        lock.release(transaction_id="tx-imposter-02")
    assert "Cannot release lock: owned by transaction" in str(exc_info.value)

    # Clean release with correct ID
    lock.release(transaction_id="tx-owner-01")


def test_workspace_lock_stale_lock_recovery(tmp_path):
    """Verifies that a stale lock from a dead PID is safely reclaimed."""
    lock_file = tmp_path / ".autodev.lock"
    # Write lock metadata with a dead PID (e.g. 999999)
    stale_meta = LockMetadata(
        owner_token="stale-token",
        transaction_id="tx-dead-pid",
        pid=999999,
        hostname=socket.gethostname(),
        ttl_seconds=300.0,
    )
    lock_file.write_text(json.dumps(stale_meta.to_dict()), encoding="utf-8")

    lock = WorkspaceLock(workspace_root=tmp_path)
    # Reclaiming stale lock must succeed
    meta = lock.acquire(transaction_id="tx-new-live-01", timeout_seconds=1.0)
    assert meta.transaction_id == "tx-new-live-01"
    assert lock.is_locked is True
    lock.release("tx-new-live-01")


# =============================================================================
# 2. PARALLEL OPERATION SCHEDULER TESTS
# =============================================================================

def test_parallel_scheduler_bounded_execution():
    """Verifies bounded parallel execution of operations across workers."""
    scheduler = ParallelOperationScheduler(max_workers=3)
    ops = [f"op_{i}" for i in range(6)]

    def _mock_work(op: str) -> str:
        time.sleep(0.01)
        return f"result_{op}"

    results = scheduler.execute_parallel_operations(ops, _mock_work)
    assert len(results) == 6
    assert results == [f"result_op_{i}" for i in range(6)]


def test_parallel_scheduler_single_or_empty():
    """Verifies parallel scheduler handles empty and single operation lists."""
    scheduler = ParallelOperationScheduler(max_workers=2)
    assert scheduler.execute_parallel_operations([], lambda x: x) == []

    single = scheduler.execute_parallel_operations(["op1"], lambda x: f"done_{x}")
    assert single == ["done_op1"]

"""
test_execution_recovery.py - Comprehensive Tests for Verified Transactional Recovery & Rollback (v2.1)
"""

import pytest
from pathlib import Path

from core.execution_journal import ExecutionJournal
from core.execution_recovery import (
    ExecutionRecovery,
    RecoveryError,
    RecoveryResult,
    RestorationVerificationError,
)
from core.execution_transaction import (
    ExecutionStatus,
    ExecutionTransaction,
    FileSnapshot,
)


# =============================================================================
# 1. TRANSACTION RECOVERY & ROLLBACK TESTS
# =============================================================================

def test_rollback_modified_files(tmp_path):
    """Verifies that modified files are cleanly restored to pre-mutation content."""
    mod_file = tmp_path / "src" / "service.py"
    mod_file.parent.mkdir(parents=True)
    mod_file.write_text("def original_function(): pass\n", encoding="utf-8")

    tx = ExecutionTransaction(
        transaction_id="tx-rec-01",
        plan_id="p1",
        task_id="t1",
        workspace_root=tmp_path,
    )
    # Capture snapshot before mutation
    tx.capture_file_snapshot("src/service.py")

    # Simulate mutation by agent
    mod_file.write_text("def broken_mutated_function(): raise Exception()\n", encoding="utf-8")
    tx.record_change("src/service.py", "MODIFY")

    recovery = ExecutionRecovery(workspace_root=tmp_path)
    res: RecoveryResult = recovery.rollback_transaction(transaction=tx)

    assert res.success is True
    assert res.verification_passed is True
    assert "src/service.py" in res.files_reverted
    assert mod_file.read_text(encoding="utf-8") == "def original_function(): pass\n"
    assert tx.status == ExecutionStatus.ROLLED_BACK


def test_rollback_created_files(tmp_path):
    """Verifies that files created during the transaction are deleted upon rollback."""
    new_file = tmp_path / "src" / "new_handler.py"

    tx = ExecutionTransaction(
        transaction_id="tx-rec-02",
        plan_id="p1",
        task_id="t1",
        workspace_root=tmp_path,
    )
    # Capture snapshot of non-existent file
    tx.capture_file_snapshot("src/new_handler.py")

    # Simulate creation
    new_file.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    new_file.write_text("class NewHandler: pass\n", encoding="utf-8")
    tx.record_change("src/new_handler.py", "CREATE")
    assert new_file.exists()

    recovery = ExecutionRecovery(workspace_root=tmp_path)
    res: RecoveryResult = recovery.rollback_transaction(transaction=tx)

    assert res.success is True
    assert res.verification_passed is True
    assert "src/new_handler.py" in res.files_deleted
    assert not new_file.exists()


def test_rollback_deleted_files(tmp_path):
    """Verifies that files deleted during transaction are restored upon rollback."""
    del_file = tmp_path / "docs" / "api.md"
    del_file.parent.mkdir(parents=True)
    del_file.write_text("# API Reference\nInitial docs content.\n", encoding="utf-8")

    tx = ExecutionTransaction(
        transaction_id="tx-rec-03",
        plan_id="p1",
        task_id="t1",
        workspace_root=tmp_path,
    )
    tx.capture_file_snapshot("docs/api.md")

    # Simulate deletion
    del_file.unlink()
    tx.record_change("docs/api.md", "DELETE")
    assert not del_file.exists()

    recovery = ExecutionRecovery(workspace_root=tmp_path)
    res: RecoveryResult = recovery.rollback_transaction(transaction=tx)

    assert res.success is True
    assert res.verification_passed is True
    assert "docs/api.md" in res.files_restored
    assert del_file.exists()
    assert del_file.read_text(encoding="utf-8") == "# API Reference\nInitial docs content.\n"


def test_rollback_idempotent_execution(tmp_path):
    """Verifies that executing rollback repeatedly is safe and idempotent."""
    target_file = tmp_path / "app.py"
    target_file.write_text("BASE_STATE = True\n", encoding="utf-8")

    tx = ExecutionTransaction(
        transaction_id="tx-rec-04",
        plan_id="p1",
        task_id="t1",
        workspace_root=tmp_path,
    )
    tx.capture_file_snapshot("app.py")
    target_file.write_text("BASE_STATE = False\n", encoding="utf-8")
    tx.record_change("app.py", "MODIFY")

    recovery = ExecutionRecovery(workspace_root=tmp_path)

    # First rollback
    res1 = recovery.rollback_transaction(transaction=tx)
    assert res1.success is True
    assert target_file.read_text(encoding="utf-8") == "BASE_STATE = True\n"

    # Second rollback
    res2 = recovery.rollback_transaction(transaction=tx)
    assert res2.success is True
    assert res2.verification_passed is True
    assert target_file.read_text(encoding="utf-8") == "BASE_STATE = True\n"


def test_rollback_with_execution_journal_logging(tmp_path):
    """Verifies that rollback operations append audit events to the ExecutionJournal."""
    journal_dir = tmp_path / "journal"
    journal = ExecutionJournal("tx-journal-rec-05", journal_root=journal_dir)

    target_file = tmp_path / "file.py"
    target_file.write_text("ORIGINAL", encoding="utf-8")

    tx = ExecutionTransaction(
        transaction_id="tx-journal-rec-05",
        plan_id="p1",
        task_id="t1",
        workspace_root=tmp_path,
    )
    tx.capture_file_snapshot("file.py")
    target_file.write_text("MUTATED", encoding="utf-8")
    tx.record_change("file.py", "MODIFY")

    recovery = ExecutionRecovery(workspace_root=tmp_path)
    res = recovery.rollback_transaction(transaction=tx, journal=journal)

    assert res.success is True
    events = journal.load_events(verify_integrity=True)
    event_types = [e.event_type for e in events]
    assert "ROLLBACK_STARTED" in event_types
    assert "FILE_REVERTED" in event_types
    assert "ROLLBACK_COMPLETED" in event_types

"""
test_execution_sandbox.py - Comprehensive Tests for Sandbox Containment & Command Policy (v2.1)
"""

import os
import sys
import pytest
from pathlib import Path

from core.execution_sandbox import (
    CommandPolicyError,
    CommandResult,
    CommandTimeoutError,
    ExecutionSandbox,
    PathContainmentError,
    ProtectedPathViolationError,
    SandboxSecurityError,
)


# =============================================================================
# 1. PATH CONTAINMENT & TRAVERSAL TESTS
# =============================================================================

def test_sandbox_valid_relative_path(tmp_path):
    """Verifies that legitimate relative paths resolve cleanly within workspace."""
    sandbox = ExecutionSandbox(workspace_root=tmp_path)
    res = sandbox.validate_path("src/core/utils.py")
    assert res == (tmp_path / "src" / "core" / "utils.py").resolve()
    assert res.is_relative_to(tmp_path)


def test_sandbox_parent_traversal_rejected(tmp_path):
    """Verifies that parent traversal attempts (../) outside root raise PathContainmentError."""
    sandbox = ExecutionSandbox(workspace_root=tmp_path)
    with pytest.raises(PathContainmentError) as exc_info:
        sandbox.validate_path("../../etc/passwd")
    assert "escapes workspace root" in str(exc_info.value).lower() or "containment violation" in str(exc_info.value).lower()


def test_sandbox_absolute_path_outside_workspace_rejected(tmp_path):
    """Verifies that absolute paths outside workspace root raise PathContainmentError."""
    sandbox = ExecutionSandbox(workspace_root=tmp_path)
    # Outside path
    outside = Path(tmp_path.parent / "other_dir" / "secret.txt")
    with pytest.raises(PathContainmentError):
        sandbox.validate_path(str(outside))


def test_sandbox_windows_drive_or_system_escape_rejected(tmp_path):
    r"""Verifies that absolute OS paths (e.g. C:\Windows or /etc) raise PathContainmentError."""
    sandbox = ExecutionSandbox(workspace_root=tmp_path)
    target = "C:\\Windows\\System32\\calc.exe" if os.name == "nt" else "/etc/shadow"
    with pytest.raises(PathContainmentError):
        sandbox.validate_path(target)


# =============================================================================
# 2. PROTECTED & SENSITIVE PATH TESTS
# =============================================================================

def test_sandbox_git_directory_mutation_forbidden(tmp_path):
    """Verifies that writing to .git control directory is prohibited."""
    sandbox = ExecutionSandbox(workspace_root=tmp_path, allow_git_control_writes=False)
    with pytest.raises(ProtectedPathViolationError) as exc_info:
        sandbox.validate_path(".git/config", is_write=True)
    assert "protected directory '.git'" in str(exc_info.value).lower()


def test_sandbox_sensitive_denied_patterns(tmp_path):
    """Verifies that credentials and secret keys (.env, id_rsa, .pem) are blocked."""
    sandbox = ExecutionSandbox(workspace_root=tmp_path)

    with pytest.raises(ProtectedPathViolationError):
        sandbox.validate_path(".env")

    with pytest.raises(ProtectedPathViolationError):
        sandbox.validate_path("config/production.env")

    with pytest.raises(ProtectedPathViolationError):
        sandbox.validate_path("id_rsa")

    with pytest.raises(ProtectedPathViolationError):
        sandbox.validate_path("certs/server.pem")


def test_sandbox_custom_allowed_paths(tmp_path):
    """Verifies that configured allowed_paths blocks writes to non-whitelisted paths."""
    sandbox = ExecutionSandbox(
        workspace_root=tmp_path,
        allowed_paths=["src", "tests", "docs"],
    )

    # Allowed paths succeed
    sandbox.validate_path("src/module.py", is_write=True)
    sandbox.validate_path("tests/test_mod.py", is_write=True)

    # Non-allowed path is rejected
    with pytest.raises(ProtectedPathViolationError) as exc_info:
        sandbox.validate_path("scripts/deploy.sh", is_write=True)
    assert "not within any configured allowed paths" in str(exc_info.value)


# =============================================================================
# 3. COMMAND POLICY TESTS
# =============================================================================

def test_sandbox_validate_command_approved_binary(tmp_path):
    """Verifies that approved command binaries are parsed into safe argument arrays."""
    sandbox = ExecutionSandbox(workspace_root=tmp_path)
    args = sandbox.validate_command("python -m py_compile src/app.py")
    assert args == ["python", "-m", "py_compile", "src/app.py"]


def test_sandbox_validate_command_unapproved_binary_rejected(tmp_path):
    """Verifies that unapproved binaries raise CommandPolicyError."""
    sandbox = ExecutionSandbox(workspace_root=tmp_path)
    with pytest.raises(CommandPolicyError) as exc_info:
        sandbox.validate_command("curl http://example.com")
    assert "not in the approved command allowlist" in str(exc_info.value)


def test_sandbox_dangerous_command_substrings_rejected(tmp_path):
    """Verifies that destructive shell commands are blocked."""
    sandbox = ExecutionSandbox(workspace_root=tmp_path)
    with pytest.raises(CommandPolicyError) as exc_info:
        sandbox.validate_command("python -c 'import os; os.system(\"rm -rf /\")'")
    assert "prohibited sequence" in str(exc_info.value).lower()


# =============================================================================
# 4. SUBPROCESS EXECUTION TESTS
# =============================================================================

def test_sandbox_run_command_success(tmp_path):
    """Verifies running a safe subprocess in the sandbox."""
    sandbox = ExecutionSandbox(workspace_root=tmp_path)

    assert res.exit_code == 0
    assert "sandbox execution successful" in res.stdout

def test_sandbox_run_command_timeout(tmp_path):

    sandbox = ExecutionSandbox(workspace_root=tmp_path)

    assert res.timed_out is True
    assert res.success is False

def test_sandbox_run_command_redacts_secrets(tmp_path):

"""
test_execution_transaction.py - Comprehensive Tests for Transaction Models & Lifecycle (v2.1)
"""

import json
import pytest
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from pathlib import Path

from core.execution_transaction import (
    ExecutionAuthorizationError,
    ExecutionEngineError,
    ExecutionReport,
    ExecutionStatus,
    ExecutionTransaction,
    FileSnapshot,
    InvalidStateTransitionError,
    OperationExecutionResult,
    StageExecutionResult,
    TransactionError,
    WorkspaceSafetyError,
    validate_state_transition,
)


# =============================================================================
# 1. STATE TRANSITION TESTS
# =============================================================================

def test_valid_state_transitions():
    """Verifies that all standard legal lifecycle transitions succeed."""
    # PENDING -> VALIDATING -> READY -> RUNNING -> SUCCEEDED
    validate_state_transition(ExecutionStatus.PENDING, ExecutionStatus.VALIDATING)
    validate_state_transition(ExecutionStatus.VALIDATING, ExecutionStatus.READY)
    validate_state_transition(ExecutionStatus.READY, ExecutionStatus.RUNNING)
    validate_state_transition(ExecutionStatus.RUNNING, ExecutionStatus.SUCCEEDED)

    # RUNNING -> ROLLING_BACK -> ROLLED_BACK
    validate_state_transition(ExecutionStatus.RUNNING, ExecutionStatus.ROLLING_BACK)
    validate_state_transition(ExecutionStatus.ROLLING_BACK, ExecutionStatus.ROLLED_BACK)

    # Self-transition is a no-op
    validate_state_transition(ExecutionStatus.RUNNING, ExecutionStatus.RUNNING)


def test_invalid_state_transitions_raise_error():
    """Verifies that illegal state transitions raise InvalidStateTransitionError."""
    # Cannot jump directly from PENDING to SUCCEEDED
    with pytest.raises(InvalidStateTransitionError) as exc_info:
        validate_state_transition(ExecutionStatus.PENDING, ExecutionStatus.SUCCEEDED)
    assert "cannot transition" in str(exc_info.value)

    # Cannot transition from terminal SUCCEEDED to RUNNING
    with pytest.raises(InvalidStateTransitionError):
        validate_state_transition(ExecutionStatus.SUCCEEDED, ExecutionStatus.RUNNING)

    # Cannot transition from CANCELLED to READY
    with pytest.raises(InvalidStateTransitionError):
        validate_state_transition(ExecutionStatus.CANCELLED, ExecutionStatus.READY)


def test_transition_to_updates_transaction_lifecycle():
    """Verifies that ExecutionTransaction.transition_to updates timestamps and status."""
    tx = ExecutionTransaction(
        transaction_id="tx-test-01",
        plan_id="plan-01",
        task_id="task-01",
        workspace_root="/workspace",
    )
    assert tx.status == ExecutionStatus.PENDING
    assert tx.completed_at is None

    tx.transition_to(ExecutionStatus.VALIDATING)
    assert tx.status == ExecutionStatus.VALIDATING

    tx.transition_to(ExecutionStatus.READY)
    assert tx.status == ExecutionStatus.READY

    tx.transition_to(ExecutionStatus.RUNNING)
    assert tx.status == ExecutionStatus.RUNNING

    tx.transition_to(ExecutionStatus.SUCCEEDED)
    assert tx.status == ExecutionStatus.SUCCEEDED
    assert tx.completed_at is not None


# =============================================================================
# 2. FILE SNAPSHOT TESTS
# =============================================================================

def test_file_snapshot_capture_existing_text(tmp_path):
    """Verifies FileSnapshot captures existing text file content, size, and SHA256 hash."""
    file_path = tmp_path / "src" / "sample.py"
    file_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True)
    file_path.write_text("print('hello world')", encoding="utf-8")

    tx = ExecutionTransaction(
        transaction_id="tx-snap-01",
        plan_id="plan-01",
        task_id="task-01",
        workspace_root=tmp_path,
    )

    snapshot = tx.capture_file_snapshot("src/sample.py")
    assert snapshot.exists_before is True
    assert snapshot.relative_path == "src/sample.py"
    assert snapshot.size_bytes_before > 0
    assert snapshot.content_hash_before is not None
    assert snapshot.is_binary is False
    assert snapshot.content_backup == "print('hello world')"


def test_file_snapshot_capture_nonexistent_file(tmp_path):
    """Verifies FileSnapshot captures non-existent file cleanly."""
    tx = ExecutionTransaction(
        transaction_id="tx-snap-02",
        plan_id="plan-01",
        task_id="task-01",
        workspace_root=tmp_path,
    )

    snapshot = tx.capture_file_snapshot("src/new_module.py")
    assert snapshot.exists_before is False
    assert snapshot.content_hash_before is None
    assert snapshot.size_bytes_before == 0
    assert snapshot.content_backup is None


def test_file_snapshot_capture_idempotent_preserves_initial_baseline(tmp_path):
    """Verifies that calling capture_file_snapshot twice preserves the original baseline."""
    file_path = tmp_path / "data.txt"
    file_path.write_text("Initial Content", encoding="utf-8")

    tx = ExecutionTransaction(
        transaction_id="tx-snap-03",
        plan_id="plan-01",
        task_id="task-01",
        workspace_root=tmp_path,
    )

    snap1 = tx.capture_file_snapshot("data.txt")
    assert snap1.content_backup == "Initial Content"

    # Mutate file on disk
    file_path.write_text("Mutated Content", encoding="utf-8")

    # Second capture must return original snapshot
    snap2 = tx.capture_file_snapshot("data.txt")
    assert snap2.content_backup == "Initial Content"
    assert snap1 is snap2


def test_file_snapshot_to_dict_and_from_dict():
    """Verifies FileSnapshot serialization roundtrip."""
    snap = FileSnapshot(
        relative_path="core/utils.py",
        absolute_path="/workspace/core/utils.py",
        exists_before=True,
        content_hash_before="abc123sha",
        size_bytes_before=150,
        is_binary=False,
    )
    data = snap.to_dict()
    restored = FileSnapshot.from_dict(data)
    assert restored.relative_path == snap.relative_path
    assert restored.content_hash_before == snap.content_hash_before
    assert restored.exists_before is True


# =============================================================================
# 3. OPERATION & STAGE RESULT TESTS
# =============================================================================

def test_operation_execution_result_roundtrip():
    """Verifies OperationExecutionResult serialization and schema defaults."""
    op_res = OperationExecutionResult(
        operation_id="OP-001",
        status=ExecutionStatus.SUCCEEDED,
        started_at="2026-10-09T00:00:00Z",
        finished_at="2026-10-09T00:00:02Z",
        duration_seconds=2.0,
        modified_files=["core/module.py"],
        created_files=["tests/test_module.py"],
        deleted_files=[],
    )
    d = op_res.to_dict()
    restored = OperationExecutionResult.from_dict(d)
    assert restored.operation_id == "OP-001"
    assert restored.status == ExecutionStatus.SUCCEEDED
    assert restored.modified_files == ["core/module.py"]
    assert restored.duration_seconds == 2.0


def test_stage_execution_result_roundtrip():
    """Verifies StageExecutionResult serialization with child operation results."""
    stage_res = StageExecutionResult(
        stage_number=1,
        status=ExecutionStatus.SUCCEEDED,
        operation_results=[
            OperationExecutionResult(
                operation_id="OP-001",
                status=ExecutionStatus.SUCCEEDED,
                duration_seconds=1.5,
            )
        ],
        validation_results={"gate-lint": {"passed": True}},
        checkpoint_id="chk-01",
        duration_seconds=1.5,
    )
    d = stage_res.to_dict()
    restored = StageExecutionResult.from_dict(d)
    assert restored.stage_number == 1
    assert restored.status == ExecutionStatus.SUCCEEDED
    assert len(restored.operation_results) == 1
    assert restored.checkpoint_id == "chk-01"


# =============================================================================
# 4. EXECUTION TRANSACTION MUTATION TRACKING
# =============================================================================

def test_execution_transaction_record_changes(tmp_path):
    """Verifies record_change tracks created, modified, and deleted files cleanly."""
    tx = ExecutionTransaction(
        transaction_id="tx-mut-01",
        plan_id="plan-01",
        task_id="task-01",
        workspace_root=tmp_path,
    )

    tx.record_change("src/a.py", "CREATE")
    assert "src/a.py" in tx.created_files
    assert "src/a.py" not in tx.modified_files

    tx.record_change("src/b.py", "MODIFY")
    assert "src/b.py" in tx.modified_files

    tx.record_change("src/c.py", "DELETE")
    assert "src/c.py" in tx.deleted_files

    # Modifying a created file stays in created_files
    tx.record_change("src/a.py", "MODIFY")
    assert "src/a.py" in tx.created_files
    assert "src/a.py" not in tx.modified_files


def test_execution_transaction_checkpoints():
    """Verifies checkpoint ID registration in transaction."""
    tx = ExecutionTransaction(
        transaction_id="tx-chk-01",
        plan_id="plan-01",
        task_id="task-01",
        workspace_root="/workspace",
    )
    tx.create_checkpoint("chk-stage-1")
    tx.create_checkpoint("chk-stage-2")
    assert tx.checkpoint_ids == ["chk-stage-1", "chk-stage-2"]


def test_execution_transaction_to_dict_and_from_dict(tmp_path):
    """Verifies full ExecutionTransaction serialization and restoration."""
    tx = ExecutionTransaction(
        transaction_id="tx-full-01",
        plan_id="plan-01",
        task_id="task-01",
        workspace_root=tmp_path,
        initial_git_head="commit-sha-1234",
    )
    tx.record_change("src/main.py", "MODIFY")
    tx.create_checkpoint("chk-01")

    data = tx.to_dict()
    restored = ExecutionTransaction.from_dict(data)

    assert restored.transaction_id == "tx-full-01"
    assert restored.initial_git_head == "commit-sha-1234"
    assert "src/main.py" in restored.modified_files
    assert "chk-01" in restored.checkpoint_ids


# =============================================================================
# 5. EXECUTION REPORT TESTS
# =============================================================================

def test_execution_report_serialization():
    """Verifies ExecutionReport serialization, JSON formatting, and deserialization."""
    report = ExecutionReport(
        transaction_id="tx-rep-01",
        overall_success=True,
        status=ExecutionStatus.SUCCEEDED,
        stages_completed=3,
        stages_failed=0,
        operations_completed=5,
        operations_failed=0,
        files_created=["src/new.py"],
        files_modified=["src/old.py"],
        files_deleted=[],
        duration_seconds=12.4,
    )

    json_str = report.to_json()
    assert '"overall_success": true' in json_str
    assert '"stages_completed": 3' in json_str

    parsed = json.loads(json_str)
    restored = ExecutionReport.from_dict(parsed)
    assert restored.transaction_id == "tx-rep-01"
    assert restored.overall_success is True
    assert restored.status == ExecutionStatus.SUCCEEDED
    assert restored.files_created == ["src/new.py"]

        assert ExecutiveRole.DIRECTOR_SECURITY in roles

        assert ceo is not None
        assert ceo.role == ExecutiveRole.CEO
        assert ceo.title == "Chief Executive Officer"
        assert ceo.budget_authority_usd >= 5000000.0

    def test_update_kpis(self, engine: ExecutiveDecisionEngine):
        engine.update_executive_kpis(ExecutiveRole.CTO, {"architecture_health": 98.5})
        cto = engine.get_executive(ExecutiveRole.CTO)
        assert cto.kpis["architecture_health"] == 98.5

    def test_propose_decision(self, engine: ExecutiveDecisionEngine):
        dec = engine.propose_decision(
            title="Adopt Rust for Core Gateway",
            description="Upgrade core routing engine to high-performance Rust service",
            proposer_role=ExecutiveRole.CTO,
            required_signoffs=[ExecutiveRole.VP_ENGINEERING, ExecutiveRole.DIRECTOR_SECURITY],
            budget_impact_usd=150000.0,
            strategic_alignment_score=92.0,
            risk_score=20.0,
        )
        assert dec.decision_id.startswith("DEC-")
        assert dec.status == DecisionStatus.PROPOSED
        assert len(dec.required_signoffs) >= 2

    def test_decision_approval_flow(self, engine: ExecutiveDecisionEngine):
        dec = engine.propose_decision(
            title="Expand AI Infrastructure Cluster",
            description="Add 32 GPU nodes for local training",
            proposer_role=ExecutiveRole.VP_ENGINEERING,
            required_signoffs=[ExecutiveRole.CTO, ExecutiveRole.DIRECTOR_FINANCE],
            budget_impact_usd=300000.0,
        )

        # First signoff
        res1 = engine.signoff_decision(dec.decision_id, ExecutiveRole.CTO, approved=True, notes="Tech stack verified")
        assert res1.status == DecisionStatus.IN_REVIEW
        assert res1.signoffs_received["CTO"] is True

        # Second signoff completes approval

        assert res2.status == DecisionStatus.APPROVED

            required_signoffs=[ExecutiveRole.VP_ENGINEERING],
            budget_impact_usd=50000.0,

        res = engine.signoff_decision(dec.decision_id, ExecutiveRole.VP_ENGINEERING, approved=False, notes="Cost exceeds target")

    def test_executive_veto(self, engine: ExecutiveDecisionEngine):

            title="Disable MFA for Automated Load Tests",
            description="Bypass security for performance benchmarking",
            proposer_role=ExecutiveRole.DIRECTOR_QA,
            required_signoffs=[ExecutiveRole.VP_ENGINEERING],
        )
        vetoed = engine.veto_decision(
            dec.decision_id,
            veto_role=ExecutiveRole.DIRECTOR_SECURITY,
            reason="Violates SOC2 compliance and zero-trust policy",
        )
        assert vetoed.status == DecisionStatus.VETOED
        assert vetoed.veto_role == ExecutiveRole.DIRECTOR_SECURITY

    def test_budget_exceeded_auto_escalation(self, engine: ExecutiveDecisionEngine):
        # Director of Documentation authority is $150,000. Proposing $500,000 decision.
        dec = engine.propose_decision(
            title="Global Translation Retainer",
            description="Contract multi-language documentation agency",
            proposer_role=ExecutiveRole.DIRECTOR_DOCUMENTATION,
            required_signoffs=[ExecutiveRole.VP_PRODUCT],
            budget_impact_usd=500000.0,
        )
        # Required signoffs should auto-include CEO and DIRECTOR_FINANCE
        assert ExecutiveRole.CEO in dec.required_signoffs
        assert ExecutiveRole.DIRECTOR_FINANCE in dec.required_signoffs

    def test_strategic_goals_management(self, engine: ExecutiveDecisionEngine):
        goal = engine.create_strategic_goal(
            goal_id="GOAL-Q1-2026-01",
            title="Autonomous Enterprise Delivery",
            description="Deliver AutoDev Version 3.0",
            target_quarter="Q1",
            target_year=2026,
            owner_role=ExecutiveRole.CEO,
            target_metric="DORA_DEPLOY_PER_DAY",
            target_value=5.0,
        )
        assert goal.goal_id == "GOAL-Q1-2026-01"
        assert goal.progress_pct == 0.0

        engine.update_strategic_goal_progress("GOAL-Q1-2026-01", current_value=4.0)
        updated = engine.get_strategic_goal("GOAL-Q1-2026-01")
        assert updated.progress_pct == 80.0

    def test_list_decisions_by_status(self, engine: ExecutiveDecisionEngine):
        d1 = engine.propose_decision("D1", "Desc", ExecutiveRole.CEO, [ExecutiveRole.CTO])
        d2 = engine.propose_decision("D2", "Desc", ExecutiveRole.CEO, [ExecutiveRole.CTO])
        engine.signoff_decision(d1.decision_id, ExecutiveRole.CTO, approved=True)

        approved_list = engine.list_decisions(status=DecisionStatus.APPROVED)
        assert any(d.decision_id == d1.decision_id for d in approved_list)
        assert not any(d.decision_id == d2.decision_id for d in approved_list)

from core.failure_classifier import FailureClassifier, FlakyTestDetector

class TestFailureClassifier(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_classify_assertion_failure(self):
        msg = "AssertionError: Expected 42, but got 41"
        ftype, conf, _ = FailureClassifier.classify(message=msg)
        self.assertEqual(ftype, FailureType.ASSERTION_FAILURE)
        self.assertGreaterEqual(conf, 0.8)

    def test_classify_syntax_error(self):
        msg = "SyntaxError: invalid syntax (main.py, line 12)"
        ftype, conf, _ = FailureClassifier.classify(message=msg)
        self.assertEqual(ftype, FailureType.SYNTAX_ERROR)
        self.assertGreaterEqual(conf, 0.9)

    def test_classify_import_error(self):
        msg = "ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'nonexistent_package'"
        ftype, conf, _ = FailureClassifier.classify(message=msg)
        self.assertEqual(ftype, FailureType.IMPORT_FAILURE)
        self.assertGreaterEqual(conf, 0.9)

    def test_classify_network_dependency(self):
        msg = "ConnectionRefusedError: [Errno 111] Connection refused on 127.0.0.1:5432"
        ftype, conf, _ = FailureClassifier.classify(message=msg)
        self.assertEqual(ftype, FailureType.NETWORK_DEPENDENCY_FAILURE)
        self.assertTrue(FailureClassifier.is_environmental(ftype))

    def test_classify_timeout(self):
        ftype, conf, _ = FailureClassifier.classify(message="Timeout", exit_code=124)
        self.assertEqual(ftype, FailureType.TEST_TIMEOUT)

    def test_classify_type_error(self):
        msg = "TypeError: unsupported operand type(s) for +: 'int' and 'str'"
        ftype, conf, _ = FailureClassifier.classify(message=msg)
        self.assertEqual(ftype, FailureType.TYPE_CHECKING_FAILURE)

    def test_classify_test_result_enrichment(self):
        test = SingleTestResult(
            test_id="test_mod",
            test_name="test_fn",
            status=TestStatus.FAILED,
            message="AssertionError: assert False",
        )
        enriched = FailureClassifier.classify_test_result(test)
        self.assertEqual(enriched.failure_type, FailureType.ASSERTION_FAILURE)


class TestFlakyTestDetector(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_flaky_detection_true(self):
        detector = FlakyTestDetector(max_retries=3)
        calls = [True, False, True]
        idx = 0

        def runner():
            nonlocal idx
            res = calls[idx % len(calls)]
            idx += 1
            return res

        is_flaky, pass_rate, _ = detector.evaluate_test(runner, "test_flaky_1")
        self.assertTrue(is_flaky)
        self.assertGreater(pass_rate, 0.0)
        self.assertLess(pass_rate, 1.0)

    def test_flaky_detection_false_consistent_pass(self):
        detector = FlakyTestDetector(max_retries=3)
        is_flaky, pass_rate, _ = detector.evaluate_test(lambda: True, "test_pass_1")
        self.assertFalse(is_flaky)
        self.assertEqual(pass_rate, 1.0)

    def test_flaky_detection_false_consistent_fail(self):
        detector = FlakyTestDetector(max_retries=3)
        is_flaky, pass_rate, _ = detector.evaluate_test(lambda: False, "test_fail_1")
        self.assertFalse(is_flaky)
        self.assertEqual(pass_rate, 0.0)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

"""
test_file_writer_agent.py - Comprehensive Unit & Security Tests for FileWriterAgent

Validates:
- Writing new files
- Creating nested directories
- Skipping identical files
- Overwriting existing files
- Backup creation (.bak)
- Path traversal & security sandbox protection
- Partial failure handling
"""

import pytest
from pathlib import Path
from agents.coder_agent import GeneratedFile, GeneratedResult
from agents.file_writer_agent import (
    FileWriterAgent,
    FileWriterError,
    PathTraversalError,
    WriteResult,
)


@pytest.fixture
def temp_workspace(tmp_path: Path) -> Path:
    """Provides a fresh isolated temporary project directory."""
    workspace = tmp_path / "test_project"
    workspace.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    return workspace


def test_write_new_files(temp_workspace: Path):
    """Verifies that new files are correctly written to the workspace."""
    writer = FileWriterAgent(project_root=temp_workspace)
    files = [
        GeneratedFile(path="README.md", content="# Test Project\n"),
        GeneratedFile(path="main.py", content="print('hello world')\n"),
    ]
    result = writer.write(files)

    assert result.success is True
    assert len(result.files_written) == 2
    assert (temp_workspace / "README.md").read_text(encoding="utf-8") == "# Test Project\n"
    assert (temp_workspace / "main.py").read_text(encoding="utf-8") == "print('hello world')\n"


def test_create_nested_directories(temp_workspace: Path):
    """Verifies that deep nested directories are created automatically."""
    writer = FileWriterAgent(project_root=temp_workspace)
    files = [
        GeneratedFile(
            path="src/api/v1/endpoints/users.py",
            content="# Users router\n",
        )
    ]
    result = writer.write(files)

    assert result.success is True
    assert (temp_workspace / "src/api/v1/endpoints/users.py").is_file()
    assert (temp_workspace / "src/api/v1/endpoints/users.py").read_text(encoding="utf-8") == "# Users router\n"


def test_skip_identical_files(temp_workspace: Path):
    """Verifies that files with identical content are skipped without rewrite."""
    target = temp_workspace / "config.py"
    target.write_text("DEBUG = True\n", encoding="utf-8")

    writer = FileWriterAgent(project_root=temp_workspace)
    files = [GeneratedFile(path="config.py", content="DEBUG = True\n")]
    result = writer.write(files)

    assert result.success is True
    assert len(result.files_written) == 0
    assert "config.py" in result.files_skipped


def test_overwrite_existing_files(temp_workspace: Path):
    """Verifies that existing files are updated when overwrite_existing=True."""
    target = temp_workspace / "version.py"
    target.write_text("VERSION = '0.1.0'\n", encoding="utf-8")

    writer = FileWriterAgent(project_root=temp_workspace, overwrite_existing=True)
    files = [GeneratedFile(path="version.py", content="VERSION = '0.2.0'\n")]
    result = writer.write(files)

    assert result.success is True
    assert len(result.files_written) == 1
    assert target.read_text(encoding="utf-8") == "VERSION = '0.2.0'\n"


def test_backup_creation_on_overwrite(temp_workspace: Path):
    """Verifies that .bak backup files are created before overwriting."""
    target = temp_workspace / "important.py"
    original_content = "# Original code\n"
    target.write_text(original_content, encoding="utf-8")

    writer = FileWriterAgent(project_root=temp_workspace, create_backups=True)
    files = [GeneratedFile(path="important.py", content="# Updated code\n")]
    result = writer.write(files)

    backup_file = temp_workspace / "important.py.bak"

    assert result.success is True
    assert len(result.backups_created) == 1
    assert backup_file.exists()
    assert backup_file.read_text(encoding="utf-8") == original_content
    assert target.read_text(encoding="utf-8") == "# Updated code\n"


def test_path_traversal_detection(temp_workspace: Path):
    """Verifies that path traversal attempts outside workspace are blocked and captured."""
    writer = FileWriterAgent(project_root=temp_workspace)
    malicious_files = [
        GeneratedFile(path="../../outside.txt", content="malicious\n"),
        GeneratedFile(path="src/valid.py", content="valid\n"),
    ]
    result = writer.write(malicious_files)

    assert result.success is False
    assert "../../outside.txt" in result.failed_files
    assert "Path traversal detected" in result.failed_files["../../outside.txt"]
    assert "src/valid.py" in result.files_written


def test_partial_failure_with_overwrite_disabled(temp_workspace: Path):
    """Verifies behavior when overwrite_existing=False and some files already exist."""
    existing_file = temp_workspace / "existing.py"
    existing_file.write_text("old content\n", encoding="utf-8")

    writer = FileWriterAgent(project_root=temp_workspace, overwrite_existing=False)
    batch = [
        GeneratedFile(path="existing.py", content="new content\n"),
        GeneratedFile(path="new_file.py", content="brand new\n"),
    ]
    result = writer.write(batch)

    assert result.success is False
    assert len(result.files_written) == 1
    assert "new_file.py" in result.files_written
    assert "existing.py" in result.failed_files
    assert "overwrite_existing is False" in result.failed_files["existing.py"]
    # Ensure original was not modified
    assert existing_file.read_text(encoding="utf-8") == "old content\n"


def test_generated_result_object_input(temp_workspace: Path):
    """Verifies that FileWriterAgent directly accepts a GeneratedResult object."""
    writer = FileWriterAgent(project_root=temp_workspace)
    gen_result = GeneratedResult(
        summary="Feature setup",
        files=[
            GeneratedFile(path="app.py", content="# App code\n"),
            GeneratedFile(path="test_app.py", content="# Test code\n"),
        ],
        explanation="Added app and test modules.",
    )
    result = writer.write(gen_result)

    assert result.success is True
    assert len(result.files_written) == 2
    assert (temp_workspace / "app.py").is_file()
    assert (temp_workspace / "test_app.py").is_file()

        entry = finance.record_expense(
            category=ExpenseCategory.LLM_API_TOKENS,
            amount_usd=5000.0,
            description="LLM API calls for code generation",
            department=DepartmentType.ENGINEERING,

            finance.record_expense(ExpenseCategory.STORAGE_CAS, -500.0, "Invalid", DepartmentType.DEVOPS)

        assert runway == 20.0

    def test_calculate_roi(self, finance: FinanceManager):
        # Invest $100k, return $300k => ((300 - 100) / 100) * 100 = 200.0%

"""
test_git_agent.py - Comprehensive Unit & Integration Tests for GitAgent

Validates:
- Repository detection with is_git_repository() and check_repository()
- Repository initialization (git init, initial branch, default .gitignore)
- Branch operations (create_branch, checkout_branch, get_current_branch)
- Working tree status parsing (clean, untracked, modified, staged)
- Staging operations (stage_all, stage_files)
- Commit execution (commit creation, get_latest_commit_hash, branch detection, telemetry)
- Empty commit prevention (clean directory returns success=False)
- Rollback operations (soft reset and hard reset via rollback_last_commit)
- Remote operations handling (push, pull without crashing on missing remote)
- Commit message synthesis (Task objects, dicts, review results with quality scores)
- Error handling on invalid repository operations
- Missing git executable and infrastructure failure handling
- Mock subprocess failures and timeout handling
- Zero network operations / remote operations safety
"""

import os
import subprocess
from pathlib import Path
from unittest.mock import MagicMock, patch
import pytest

from agents.git_agent import (
    CommitFailureError,
    CommitResult,
    GitAgent,
    GitAgentException,
    GitCommandError,
    GitExecutableNotFoundError,
    GitOperationError,
    GitOperationResult,
    GitStatus,
    RepositoryNotFoundError,
)


@pytest.fixture
def temp_workspace(tmp_path: Path) -> Path:
    """Provides an isolated clean workspace directory."""
    ws = tmp_path / "test_repo"
    ws.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    return ws


@pytest.fixture
def initialized_git_repo(temp_workspace: Path) -> GitAgent:
    """Provides a GitAgent initialized with an active local Git repository."""
    agent = GitAgent(
        project_root=temp_workspace,
        auto_init=True,
        user_name="AutoDev Tester",
        user_email="tester@autodev.local",
    )
    return agent


# =============================================================================
# 1. Repository Detection & Initialization Tests
# =============================================================================

def test_check_repository_on_empty_directory(temp_workspace: Path):
    """Verifies that is_git_repository returns False for an uninitialized folder."""
    agent = GitAgent(project_root=temp_workspace, auto_init=False)
    assert agent.is_git_repository() is False
    assert agent.check_repository() is False


def test_initialize_repository_creates_git_and_gitignore(temp_workspace: Path):
    """Verifies that initialize_repository initializes git and writes .gitignore."""
    agent = GitAgent(project_root=temp_workspace, auto_init=False)
    assert agent.is_git_repository() is False

    res = agent.initialize_repository(initial_branch="main")
    assert isinstance(res, GitOperationResult)
    assert res.success is True
    assert agent.is_git_repository() is True
    assert (temp_workspace / ".git").is_dir()
    assert (temp_workspace / ".gitignore").is_file()


def test_initialize_repository_idempotent_on_existing_repo(initialized_git_repo: GitAgent):
    """Verifies that re-running initialization on an existing repo succeeds safely."""
    assert initialized_git_repo.is_git_repository() is True
    res = initialized_git_repo.initialize_repository()
    assert res.success is True
    assert res.data.get("already_exists") is True


# =============================================================================
# 2. Branch Operations Tests
# =============================================================================

def test_create_and_checkout_branch(initialized_git_repo: GitAgent, temp_workspace: Path):

def test_mock_subprocess_failure_returns_structured_commit_result(initialized_git_repo: GitAgent, temp_workspace: Path):
    """Verifies that unexpected subprocess errors during commit return CommitResult with error."""
    (temp_workspace / "data.py").write_text("data", encoding="utf-8")

    original_run = initialized_git_repo._run_git_command

    def mock_run(args, **kwargs):
        if len(args) > 0 and args[0] == "commit":
            raise GitCommandError(
                command="git commit",
                exit_code=128,
                stdout="",
                stderr="fatal: mock internal git error",

        return original_run(args, **kwargs)

        assert "fatal: mock internal git error" in result.error

"""

import time

import pytest

from core.certificate_manager import CertificateManager
from core.grpc_worker_client import GrpcWorkerClient
from core.grpc_worker_server import GrpcWorkerServer
from core.task_lease_manager import TaskLeaseManager
from core.worker_protocol import (

@pytest.fixture
def test_certs(tmp_path):

def test_grpc_server_client_lifecycle_plaintext(tmp_path):
    registry = WorkerRegistry()

    server = GrpcWorkerServer(
        host="127.0.0.1",
        port=0,
        registry=registry,
        lease_manager=lease_manager,

    server.start()
